ततोस्य विपुलां वृक्षं प्राक्षिपत् सागराम्भसि ।
सह तेनैव वृक्षेण पतितास्म्यहमाकुला ॥
39.m: Then the monkey threw the [tree] trunk into the waters of the ocean, / and together with that very tree, I fell down, bewildered.

39.s:
tataḥ plavaṅgamo vakṣaṃ prākṣipat sāgarāmbhasi /
saha tenaiva vṛkṣeṇa patitāsmyahamākulā //
39.d:
ततः प्लवङ्गमो वक्षं प्राक्षिपत् सागराम्भसि ।
सह तेनैव वृक्षेण पतितास्म्यहमाकुला ॥
39.m: Then all beings, both stationary and moving, / saw the tree falling by chance from the vault of heaven.

39.s:
tatombaratalād vṛkṣaṃ nipatantaṃ yadṛcchayā /
dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni stāvarāṇi carāṇi ca //
39.d:
ततोम्बरतलाद् वृक्षं निपतन्तं यदृच्छया ।
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि स्तावराणि चराणि च ॥
39.m: Then a cry of distress was raised by people seeing me fall, / and Siddhas and Gandharvas said: "Alas! This is the noble-minded

39.s:
tato hāhākṛtaṃ lokairmā patantīṃ nirīkṣya hi /
ūcuśca siddhagandharvāḥ kaṣṭaṃ seyaṃ mahātmanaḥ //
39.d:
ततो हाहाकृतं लोकैर्मा पतन्तीं निरीक्ष्य हि ।
ऊचुश्च सिद्धगन्धर्वाः कष्टं सेयं महात्मनः ॥
39.m: Indradyumna's queen, declared so by Brahmā himself— / the hero, son of Manu, performer of a thousand sacrifices!"

39.s:
indradyumnasya mahiṣī gaditā brahmaṇā svayam /
manoḥ putrasya vīrasya sahasrakratuyājinaḥ //
39.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नस्य महिषी गदिता ब्रह्मणा स्वयम् ।
मनोः पुत्रस्य वीरस्य सहस्रक्रतुयाजिनः ॥
39.m: Hearing those sweet words, I then fell into a faint; / and I do not know by whom that tree was cut into a thousand pieces.

39.s:
tāṃ vāṇīṃ madhurāṃ śrutvā mohamasmyāgatā tataḥ /
na ca jāne sa kenāpi vṛkṣaśchinnaḥ sahasradhā //
39.d:
तां वाणीं मधुरां श्रुत्वा मोहमस्म्यागता ततः ।
न च जाने स केनापि वृक्षश्छिन्नः सहस्रधा ॥
39.m: Then I was swiftly carried away by the powerful [wind], the friend of fire; / I was brought to this place, and today, fair lady, you have been seen [by me].

39.s:
tato 'smi vegād balinā hṛtānalasakhena hi /
samānītāsmayahamimaṃ tvaṃ dṛṣṭā cādya sundari //
39.d:
ततो ऽस्मि वेगाद् बलिना हृतानलसखेन हि ।
समानीतास्मयहमिमं त्वं दृष्टा चाद्य सुन्दरि ॥
39.m: Therefore arise, let the two of us go and ask who these two girls are / standing [there]; for I behold two maidens on the northern bank of Puṣkara.

39.s:
taduttaṣṭhasva gacchāvaḥ pucchāvaḥ ka ime sthite /
kanyake anupaśye hi puṇkarasyottare taṭe //
39.d:
तदुत्तष्ठस्व गच्छावः पुच्छावः क इमे स्थिते ।
कन्यके अनुपश्ये हि पुण्करस्योत्तरे तटे ॥
39.m: Having spoken thus, that fair-limbed woman, together with the slender-bodied maiden, / went eagerly to see and inquire into the business of the two maidens.

39.s:
evamuktvā varāṅgī sā tayā sutanukanyayā /
jagāma kanyake draṣṭuṃ praṣṭuṃ kāryasamutsukā //
39.d:
एवमुक्त्वा वराङ्गी सा तया सुतनुकन्यया ।
जगाम कन्यके द्रष्टुं प्रष्टुं कार्यसमुत्सुका ॥
39.m: Having gone there, she asked them, and both replied; / the true account was told by the two of them, revealing their identity.

39.s:
tato gatvā paryapucchat te ūcaturubhe api /
yāthātathyaṃ tayostābhyāṃ svamātmānaṃ niveditam //
39.d:
ततो गत्वा पर्यपुच्छत् ते ऊचतुरुभे अपि ।
याथातथ्यं तयोस्ताभ्यां स्वमात्मानं निवेदितम् ॥
39.m: Then all four of them, having reached the waters of Saptagodāvara in this world, / stay at the tīrtha, worshiping Hāṭakeśvara.

39.s:
tatastāśturopīha saptagodāvaraṃ jalam /
saṃprāpya tīrthe piṣṭhanti arcantyo hāṭakeśvaram //
39.d:
ततस्ताश्तुरोपीह सप्तगोदावरं जलम् ।
संप्राप्य तीर्थे पिष्ठन्ति अर्चन्त्यो हाटकेश्वरम् ॥
39.m: Then those three men wandered for many cycles of years / for their sake: Śakuni, Jābāli, along with Ṛtadhvaja.

39.s:
tato bahūn varṣagaṇān babhramuste janāstrayaḥ /
tāsāmarthāya śakunirjābāliḥ saṛtadhvajaḥ //
39.d:
ततो बहून् वर्षगणान् बभ्रमुस्ते जनास्त्रयः ।
तासामर्थाय शकुनिर्जाबालिः सऋतध्वजः ॥
39.m: Then the bearer of burdens, dejected when a period of ten centuries / had passed, went out of despondency along with his father to Śākala.

39.s:
bhāravāhī tataḥ khinno daśabdaśatike gate /
kāle jagāma nirvedāt samaṃ pitrā tu śākalam //
39.d:
भारवाही ततः खिन्नो दशब्दशतिके गते ।
काले जगाम निर्वेदात् समं पित्रा तु शाकलम् ॥
39.m: In that [city] the illustrious king Indradyumna, son of Manu, / was residing; having learned of [their arrival], he went out with an arghya vessel in hand.

39.s:
tasminnarapatiḥ śrīmānindradyumno manoḥ sutaḥ /
samadhyāste sa vijñāya sārghapātro viniryayau //
39.d:
तस्मिन्नरपतिः श्रीमानिन्द्रद्युम्नो मनोः सुतः ।
समध्यास्ते स विज्ञाय सार्घपात्रो विनिर्ययौ ॥
39.m: Ṛtadhvaja, together with Jābāli, was duly honored by him, / and that wise son of Ikṣvāku, Śakuni, his brother's son, was honored.

39.s:
samyak saṃpūjitastena sajābālirṛtadhvajaḥ /
sa cekṣvākusuto dhīmān śakunirbhrātṛjorcitaḥ //
39.d:
सम्यक् संपूजितस्तेन सजाबालिरृतध्वजः ।
स चेक्ष्वाकुसुतो धीमान् शकुनिर्भ्रातृजोर्चितः ॥
39.m: Then the sage Ṛtadhvaja addressed these words to Indradyumna: / "O king, our woman known as Nandayantī is lost.

39.s:
tato vākyaṃ muniḥ prāha indradyumnaṃ ṛtadhvajaḥ /
rājan naṣṭa'balāsmākaṃ nandayantīti viśrutā //
39.d:
ततो वाक्यं मुनिः प्राह इन्द्रद्युम्नं ऋतध्वजः ।
राजन् नष्टऽबलास्माकं नन्दयन्तीति विश्रुता ॥
39.m: And for her sake the earth has been traversed by us, O king; / therefore arise, search! You ought to render assistance."

39.s:
tasyārthe caiva vasudhā smābhiraṭitā nṛpa /
tasmāduttiṣṭha mārgasva sāhāyyaṃ kartumarhasi //
39.d:
तस्यार्थे चैव वसुधा स्माभिरटिता नृप ।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ मार्गस्व साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
39.m: Then the king said: "O Brahmin, my foremost woman too / is lost, though great exertion was made; to whom shall I tell of her?

39.s:
athovāca nṛpo brahman mamāpi lalanottamā /
naṣṭā kṛtaśramasyāpi kasyāhaṃ kathayāmi tām //
39.d:
अथोवाच नृपो ब्रह्मन् ममापि ललनोत्तमा ।
नष्टा कृतश्रमस्यापि कस्याहं कथयामि ताम् ॥
39.m: Falling from the sky like a mountain, that excellent tree, / upon hearing the words of the Siddhas, was split into a thousand pieces with arrows by me.

39.s:
ākāśāt parpatākāraḥ patamāno najottamaḥ /
siddhānāṃ vākyamākarṇya bāṇaiśchinnaḥ sahasradhā //
39.d:
आकाशात् पर्पताकारः पतमानो नजोत्तमः ।
सिद्धानां वाक्यमाकर्ण्य बाणैश्छिन्नः सहस्रधा ॥
39.m: And that woman of fair hips was not injured, through my deftness; / but I do not know where she is; therefore I will go to search."

39.s:
na caiva sā varārohā vibhinnā lāghāvānmayā /
na ca jānāmi sā kutra tasmād gacchāmi mārgitum //
39.d:
न चैव सा वरारोहा विभिन्ना लाघावान्मया ।
न च जानामि सा कुत्र तस्माद् गच्छामि मार्गितुम् ॥
39.m: Having spoken thus, the king, arising in haste, / gave chariots to the two twice-borns and to his brother's son.

39.s:
ityemuktvā sa nṛpaḥ samutthāya tvarānvitaḥ /
syandanāni dvijābhyāṃ sa bhrātṛputrāya cārpayat //
39.d:
इत्येमुक्त्वा स नृपः समुत्थाय त्वरान्वितः ।
स्यन्दनानि द्विजाभ्यां स भ्रातृपुत्राय चार्पयत् ॥
39.m: Mounting the chariots, swiftly searching the earth in turn, / they reached the hermitage of Badarī and saw a treasure of austerities,

39.s:
te 'dhiruhya rathāṃstūrṇaṃ mārgante vasudhāṃ kramāt /
badaryāśramamāsādya dadṛśustapasāṃ nidhim //
39.d:
ते ऽधिरुह्य रथांस्तूर्णं मार्गन्ते वसुधां क्रमात् ।
बदर्याश्रममासाद्य ददृशुस्तपसां निधिम् ॥
39.m: emaciated by asceticism, wretched, bearing matted locks caked with mud and dirt, / engrossed in sighs and fatigue, remaining in the first period of his youth.

39.s:
tapasā karśitaṃ dīnaṃ malapaṅkajaṭādharam /
niḥśvāsāyāsaparamaṃ prathame vayasi sthitam //
39.d:
तपसा कर्शितं दीनं मलपङ्कजटाधरम् ।
निःश्वासायासपरमं प्रथमे वयसि स्थितम् ॥
39.m: Approaching him, King Indradyumna, the mighty-armed, said: / "O ascetic, in your youth you have undertaken severe austerities, very hard to perform.

39.s:
tamupetyābravīd rājā indradyumno mahābhujaḥ /
tapasvin yauvane ghoramāsthito 'si suduścaram //
39.d:
तमुपेत्याब्रवीद् राजा इन्द्रद्युम्नो महाभुजः ।
तपस्विन् यौवने घोरमास्थितो ऽसि सुदुश्चरम् ॥
39.m: For what purpose is this asceticism? Tell that; let what you desire be spoken." / He replied: "Who are you? Tell me yourself, as a friend,

39.s:
tapaḥ kimarthaṃ tacchaṃsa kimabhipretamucyatām /
so 'bravīt ko bhavān brūhi mamātmānaṃ suhṛttayā //
39.d:
तपः किमर्थं तच्छंस किमभिप्रेतमुच्यताम् ।
सो ऽब्रवीत् को भवान् ब्रूहि ममात्मानं सुहृत्तया ॥
39.m: who inquires of me, afflicted by grief, exhausted, and devoted to penance." / The king said: "O ascetic, I am the lord of the earth in the city of Śākala,

39.s:
paripṛcchasi śokārtaṃ parikhinnaṃ taponvitam /
sa prāha rājāsmi vibho tapasvin śākale pure //
39.d:
परिपृच्छसि शोकार्तं परिखिन्नं तपोन्वितम् ।
स प्राह राजास्मि विभो तपस्विन् शाकले पुरे ॥
39.m: the son of Manu, the dear brother of Ikṣvāku; this has been told to you." / And the king related all of his former story to him.

39.s:
manoḥ putraḥ priyo bhrātā ikṣvākoḥ kathitaṃ tava /
sa cāsmai pūrvacaritaṃ sarvaṃ kathitavān nṛpaḥ //
39.d:
मनोः पुत्रः प्रियो भ्राता इक्ष्वाकोः कथितं तव ।
स चास्मै पूर्वचरितं सर्वं कथितवान् नृपः ॥
39.m: Having heard it, the royal sage said: "Do not abandon your body! / Come, I am going to search for the slender-limbed woman; you are my brother's son."

39.s:
śrutvā provāca rājarṣirmā muñcasva kalevaram /
āgaccha yāmi tanvaṅgīṃ vicetuṃ bhrātṛjo 'si me //
39.d:
श्रुत्वा प्रोवाच राजर्षिर्मा मुञ्चस्व कलेवरम् ।
आगच्छ यामि तन्वङ्गीं विचेतुं भ्रातृजो ऽसि मे ॥
39.m: Having spoken thus and embraced the king whose veins stood out, / quickly mounting him on a chariot, he introduced him to the two ascetics.

39.s:
ityuktvā saṃpariṣvajya nṛpaṃ dhamanisaṃtatam /
samāropya rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ tāpasābhyāṃ nyavedayat //
39.d:
इत्युक्त्वा संपरिष्वज्य नृपं धमनिसंततम् ।
समारोप्य रथं तूर्णं तापसाभ्यां न्यवेदयत् ॥
39.m: Ṛtadhvaja, along with his son, having seen that lord of the earth, / said: "Come, O king, come! I will do what is pleasing to you.

39.s:
ṛtadhvajaḥ saputrastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛthivīpatim /
provāca rājannehyohi kariṣyāmi tava priyam //
39.d:
ऋतध्वजः सपुत्रस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा पृथिवीपतिम् ।
प्रोवाच राजन्नेह्योहि करिष्यामि तव प्रियम् ॥
39.m: She who is named Citrāṅgadā, who was seen by you at Naimiṣa, / was dispatched by me alone to the Saptagodāvara tīrtha.

39.s:
yāsau citrāṅgadā nāma tvayā dṛṣṭā hi naimiṣe /
saptagodāvaraṃ tīrthaṃ sā mayaiva visarjitā //
39.d:
यासौ चित्राङ्गदा नाम त्वया दृष्टा हि नैमिषे ।
सप्तगोदावरं तीर्थं सा मयैव विसर्जिता ॥
39.m: Therefore come, let us go for the sake of the son of Sudeva; / there three other maidens will meet with ours."

39.s:
tadāgacchatha gacchamaḥ saudevasyaiva kāraṇāt /
tatrāsmākaṃ sameṣyanti kanyāstisrastathāparāḥ //
39.d:
तदागच्छथ गच्छमः सौदेवस्यैव कारणात् ।
तत्रास्माकं समेष्यन्ति कन्यास्तिस्रस्तथापराः ॥
39.m: Having spoken thus and consoled the son of Sudeva, / placing Śakuni in front, the sage together with his son and Indradyumna

39.s:
ityevamuktvā sa ṛṣiḥ samāśvāsya sudevajam /
śakuniṃ puratajha kṛtvā sendradyumnaḥ saputrakaḥ //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स ऋषिः समाश्वास्य सुदेवजम् ।
शकुनिं पुरतझ कृत्वा सेन्द्रद्युम्नः सपुत्रकः ॥
39.m: began to travel by a horse-drawn chariot / to the Saptagodāvara tīrtha, where those maidens had gone.

39.s:
syandanenāśvayuktena gantuṃ samupacakrame /
saptagodāvaraṃ tīrthaṃ yatra tāḥ kanyakā gatāḥ //
39.d:
स्यन्दनेनाश्वयुक्तेन गन्तुं समुपचक्रमे ।
सप्तगोदावरं तीर्थं यत्र ताः कन्यका गताः ॥
39.m: In the meantime, the slender Ghṛtācī, filled with grief, / wandered about the Udaya mountain, searching for her own daughter.

39.s:
etasminnantare tanvī ghṛtācī śokasaṃyutā /
vicacārodayagiriṃ vicinvantī sutāṃ nijām //
39.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तन्वी घृताची शोकसंयुता ।
विचचारोदयगिरिं विचिन्वन्ती सुतां निजाम् ॥
39.m: And the Apsaras approached that monkey and asked: / "Has the girl not been seen by you? O monkey, speak the truth to me!"

39.s:
tamāsasāda ca kapiṃ paryapṛcchat tathāpsarāḥ /
kiṃ bālā na tvayā dṛṣṭā kape satyaṃ vadasva māṃ //
39.d:
तमाससाद च कपिं पर्यपृच्छत् तथाप्सराः ।
किं बाला न त्वया दृष्टा कपे सत्यं वदस्व मां ॥
39.m: Hearing her words, the monkey said concerning the girl: / "She was seen, named Devavatī, and placed by me in a great hermitage,

39.s:
tasyāstad vacanaṃ śrutvā sakapiḥ prāha bālikām /
dṛṣṭā devavatī nāmnā mayā nyastā mahāśrame //
39.d:
तस्यास्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सकपिः प्राह बालिकाम् ।
दृष्टा देववती नाम्ना मया न्यस्ता महाश्रमे ॥
39.m: at the pure tīrtha of the Kālindī, frequented by beasts and birds, / in front of the abode of Śrīkaṇṭha; the truth has been spoken by me to you."

39.s:
kālindyā vimale tīrthe mṛgapakṣisamanvite /
śrakaṇṭhāyatanasyāgre mayā satyaṃ tavoditam //
39.d:
कालिन्द्या विमले तीर्थे मृगपक्षिसमन्विते ।
श्रकण्ठायतनस्याग्रे मया सत्यं तवोदितम् ॥
39.m: She said: "O lord of monkeys, her name is Vedavatī, / she is indeed not renowned as Devavatī; therefore come, let us two go."

39.s:
sā prāha vānarapate nāmnā vedavatīti sā /
na hi devavatī khyātā tadāccha vrajāvahe //
39.d:
सा प्राह वानरपते नाम्ना वेदवतीति सा ।
न हि देववती ख्याता तदाच्छ व्रजावहे ॥
39.m: Hearing these words of Ghṛtācī, the monkey, quickening his pace, / followed behind her toward the Kauśikī river.

39.s:
ghṛtācyāstadvacaḥ śrutvā vānarastvaritakramaḥ /
pṛṣṭhato 'syāḥ samāgacchannadīmanveva kauśikīm //
39.d:
घृताच्यास्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा वानरस्त्वरितक्रमः ।
पृष्ठतो ऽस्याः समागच्छन्नदीमन्वेव कौशिकीम् ॥
39.m: And those three foremost royal sages, / together with the two ascetics, also reached the Kauśikī in extremely swift chariots.

39.s:
te cāpi kauśikīṃ prāptā rājarṣipravarāstrayaḥ /
dvitaye tāpasābhyāṃ ca rathaiḥ paramavegibhiḥ //
39.d:
ते चापि कौशिकीं प्राप्ता राजर्षिप्रवरास्त्रयः ।
द्वितये तापसाभ्यां च रथैः परमवेगिभिः ॥
39.m: Having descended from the chariots, they came to the river to bathe; / Ghṛtācī also came to the sacred river to bathe.

39.s:
avatīrya rathebhyaste snātumabhyāgaman nadīm /
ghṛtācyapi nadīṃ snātaṃ supaṇyamājagāma ha //
39.d:
अवतीर्य रथेभ्यस्ते स्नातुमभ्यागमन् नदीम् ।
घृताच्यपि नदीं स्नातं सुपण्यमाजगाम ह ॥
39.m: The monkey followed right behind her and was seen by Jābāli; / seeing him, [Jābāli said] to his father and the mighty king:

39.s:
tāmanveva kapiḥ prāyād dṛṣṭo jābālinā tathā /
dṛṣṭvaiva pitaraṃ pārthivaṃ ca mahābalam //
39.d:
तामन्वेव कपिः प्रायाद् दृष्टो जाबालिना तथा ।
दृष्ट्वैव पितरं पार्थिवं च महाबलम् ॥
39.m: "Here comes again that swift monkey, dear father, / by whom I was previously tied by force to a tree by my matted hair!"

39.s:
sa yeva punarāyāti vānarastāta vegavān /
pūrvaṃ jaṭāsveva balādyona baddho 'smi pādape //
39.d:
स येव पुनरायाति वानरस्तात वेगवान् ।
पूर्वं जटास्वेव बलाद्योन बद्धो ऽस्मि पादपे ॥
39.m: Hearing those words of Jābāli, Śakuni, filled with anger, / took up his bow along with an arrow and spoke these words:

39.s:
tajjābālivacaḥ śrutvā śakuniḥ krodhasaṃyutaḥ /
saśaraṃ dhanurādāya idaṃ vacanamabravīt //
39.d:
तज्जाबालिवचः श्रुत्वा शकुनिः क्रोधसंयुतः ।
सशरं धनुरादाय इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
39.m: "O Brahmin, let command be given to me! Dear father, tell me, / so that I may slay this monkey today with a single arrow!"

39.s:
brahman pradīyatāṃ mahyamājñā tāta vadasva māma /
yāvadenaṃ nihanmyadya śareṇaikena vānaram //
39.d:
ब्रह्मन् प्रदीयतां मह्यमाज्ञा तात वदस्व माम ।
यावदेनं निहन्म्यद्य शरेणैकेन वानरम् ॥
39.m: When these words were spoken, the great sage, devoted to the welfare of all beings, / spoke great words endowed with reason to Śakuni:

39.s:
ityevamukte vacane sarvabhūtahite rataḥ /
maharṣiḥ śakuniṃ prāha detuyuktaṃ vaco mahat //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने सर्वभूतहिते रतः ।
महर्षिः शकुनिं प्राह देतुयुक्तं वचो महत् ॥
39.m:
When these words were spoken, the great sage, devoted to the welfare of all beings,
spoke momentous words endowed with reason to Śakuni.

39.s:
na kaścittāta kenāpi badhyate hanyate 'pi vā /
vadhabandhau pūrvakarmavaśyau nṛpatinandana //
39.d:
न कश्चित्तात केनापि बध्यते हन्यते ऽपि वा ।
वधबन्धौ पूर्वकर्मवश्यौ नृपतिनन्दन ॥
39.m: "No one, dear child, is bound by anyone, nor is anyone slain; / slaying and bondage are subject to previous action, prince."

39.s:
ityevamuktvā śakunimṛṣirvānaramabravīt /
ehyehi vānarāsmākaṃ sāhāyyaṃ kartumarhasi //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा शकुनिमृषिर्वानरमब्रवीत् ।
एह्येहि वानरास्माकं साहाय्यं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
39.m: Having spoken thus to Śakuni, the sage addressed the monkey: / "Come, come, monkey! You ought to render us assistance."

39.s:
ityevamukto muninā bāle sa kapikuñjaraḥ /
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā praṇipatyedamabravīt/ /
mamājñā dīyatāṃ brahman śādhi kiṃ karavāṇyaham //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्तो मुनिना बाले स कपिकुञ्जरः ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा प्रणिपत्येदमब्रवीत्। ।
ममाज्ञा दीयतां ब्रह्मन् शाधि किं करवाण्यहम् ॥
39.m: Being addressed thus by the sage, that foremost of monkeys, O young woman, / folding his hands in reverence and bowing down, spoke this: / "Give me your command, O Brahmin! Instruct me: what shall I do?"

39.s:
ityakte prāha sa munistaṃ vānarapatiṃ vacaḥ /
mama putrastvayodbaddho jaṭāsu vaṭapādape //
39.d:
इत्यक्ते प्राह स मुनिस्तं वानरपतिं वचः ।
मम पुत्रस्त्वयोद्बद्धो जटासु वटपादपे ॥
39.m: When this was said, that sage addressed words to the lord of monkeys: / "My son was bound by you in his matted hair to a banyan tree;

39.s:
na conmocayituṃ vṛkṣācchaknuyāmo 'pi yatnataḥ /
tadanena narendreṇa tridhā kṛtvā tu śākhinaḥ //
39.d:
न चोन्मोचयितुं वृक्षाच्छक्नुयामो ऽपि यत्नतः ।
तदनेन नरेन्द्रेण त्रिधा कृत्वा तु शाखिनः ॥
39.m: and even with effort we cannot release him from the tree. / Therefore, this king having cut the tree into three parts,

39.s:
śākhāṃ vahati matsūnuḥ śirasā tāṃ vimocaya /
daśavarṣaśatānyasya śākhāṃ vai vahato 'gaman //
39.d:
शाखां वहति मत्सूनुः शिरसा तां विमोचय ।
दशवर्षशतान्यस्य शाखां वै वहतो ऽगमन् ॥
39.m: my son bears the branch upon his head; release him [from it]! / Indeed, a thousand years have passed while he carried the branch,

39.s:
na ca so 'sti pumān kaścid yaco hyunmocayituṃ kṣamaḥ /
sa ṛṣervākyamākarṇya kapirjābālino jaṭāḥ //
39.d:
न च सो ऽस्ति पुमान् कश्चिद् यचो ह्युन्मोचयितुं क्षमः ।
स ऋषेर्वाक्यमाकर्ण्य कपिर्जाबालिनो जटाः ॥
39.m: and there is no man who is able to release it." / Hearing the sage's words, the monkey [untied] Jābāli's matted hair;

39.s:
śanairunmocayāmāsa kṣaṇādunmocitāśca tāḥ /
tataḥ prīto muniśreṣṭho varadobhūdṛtadhjaḥ //
39.d:
शनैरुन्मोचयामास क्षणादुन्मोचिताश्च ताः ।
ततः प्रीतो मुनिश्रेष्ठो वरदोभूदृतध्जः ॥
39.m: he untied it slowly, and in an instant it was released. / Then, delighted, Ṛtadhvaja, foremost of sages, became a giver of boons;

39.s:
kapiṃ prāha vṛṇiṣva tvaṃ varaṃ yanmanasopsitam /
ṛtadhvajavacaḥ śrutvā imaṃ varamayācata //
39.d:
कपिं प्राह वृणिष्व त्वं वरं यन्मनसोप्सितम् ।
ऋतध्वजवचः श्रुत्वा इमं वरमयाचत ॥
39.m: he said to the monkey: "Choose whatever boon your heart desires!" / Hearing Ṛtadhvaja's words, he asked for this boon:

39.s:
viśvakarmā mahātejāḥ kapitve pratisaṃsthitaḥ /
brahman bhavānvaraṃ mahyaṃ yadi dātumihecchati //
39.d:
विश्वकर्मा महातेजाः कपित्वे प्रतिसंस्थितः ।
ब्रह्मन् भवान्वरं मह्यं यदि दातुमिहेच्छति ॥
39.m: Viśvakarman of great splendour, abiding in monkey form, [said:] / "O Brahmin, if you wish to grant me a boon here,

39.s:
tatsvadatto mahāghoro mama śāpo nivartyatām /
citrāṅgadāyāḥ pitaraṃ māṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ tapodhana //
abhijānīhi bhavataḥ śāpādvāratāṃ gatm /
subahūni ca pāpāni mayā yāni kṛtāni hi //
39.d:
तत्स्वदत्तो महाघोरो मम शापो निवर्त्यताम् ।
चित्राङ्गदायाः पितरं मां त्वष्टारं तपोधन ॥
अभिजानीहि भवतः शापाद्वारतां गत्म् ।
सुबहूनि च पापानि मया यानि कृतानि हि ॥
39.m:
then let the terrible curse given by yourself to me be revoked! / Know me, O ascetic, as Tvaṣṭṛ, the father of Citrāṅgadā,

who became a monkey on account of your curse. / And whatever numerous sins have been committed by me

39.s:
kapicāpalyadoṣeṇa tāni me yāntu saṃkṣyam /
tato ṛthadhvajaḥ prāha śāpasyānto bhaviṣyati //
39.d:
कपिचापल्यदोषेण तानि मे यान्तु संक्ष्यम् ।
ततो ऋथध्वजः प्राह शापस्यान्तो भविष्यति ॥
39.m: through the fault of a monkey's fickleness, let them go to destruction!" / Thereupon Ṛtadhvaja said: "The end of the curse will come

39.s:
yadā ghṛtācyāṃ tanayaṃ janiṣyasi mahābalam /
ityevamuktāḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sa tadā kapikuñjaraḥ //
39.d:
यदा घृताच्यां तनयं जनिष्यसि महाबलम् ।
इत्येवमुक्ताः संहृष्टः स तदा कपिकुञ्जरः ॥
39.m: when you beget a son of great strength upon Ghṛtācī." / Being spoken to thus, that foremost of monkeys was delighted then.

39.s:
snātuṃ tūrṇaṃ mahānadyāmavatīrṇaḥ kṛśodari /
tatastu sarve kramāśaḥ snātvār'cya pitṛdevatāḥ //
39.d:
स्नातुं तूर्णं महानद्यामवतीर्णः कृशोदरि ।
ततस्तु सर्वे क्रमाशः स्नात्वार्ऽच्य पितृदेवताः ॥
39.m: He quickly descended into the great river to bathe, O slender-waisted lady. / Then all of them, having bathed in succession and worshipped the ancestors and gods,

39.s:
jagmurhṛṣṭā rathebhyaste ghṛtācī divamutpatat /
tāmanveva mahāvegaḥ sa kapiḥ plavatāṃ varaḥ //
dadṛśe rūpasaṃpannāṃ ghṛtācīṃ sa plavaṅgamaḥ /
sāpi taṃ balināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva kapikuñjaram //
39.d:
जग्मुर्हृष्टा रथेभ्यस्ते घृताची दिवमुत्पतत् ।
तामन्वेव महावेगः स कपिः प्लवतां वरः ॥
ददृशे रूपसंपन्नां घृताचीं स प्लवङ्गमः ।
सापि तं बलिनां श्रेष्ठं दृष्ट्वैव कपिकुञ्जरम् ॥
39.m:
went gladly to their chariots; and Ghṛtācī flew up to heaven. / Following after her with great speed, that monkey, best of jumpers,

the monkey beheld Ghṛtācī endowed with beauty. / She too, upon seeing that foremost of monkeys, best of the mighty,

39.s:
jñātvāthata viśvakarmāṇaṃ kāmayāmāsa kāminī /
tato 'nu parvataśreṣṭhe khyāte kolāhale kapiḥ //
39.d:
ज्ञात्वाथत विश्वकर्माणं कामयामास कामिनी ।
ततो ऽनु पर्वतश्रेष्ठे ख्याते कोलाहले कपिः ॥
39.m: and knowing him then to be Viśvakarman, the passionate woman desired him. / Then, upon that best of mountains known as Kolāhala, the monkey

39.s:
ramayāmāsa tāṃ tanvīṃ sā ca taṃ vānarottamam /
evaṃ ramantau suciraṃ saṃprāptau vindhyaparvatam //
39.d:
रमयामास तां तन्वीं सा च तं वानरोत्तमम् ।
एवं रमन्तौ सुचिरं संप्राप्तौ विन्ध्यपर्वतम् ॥
39.m: delighted that slender lady, and she delighted that best of monkeys. / Sporting thus for a very long time, they reached the Vindhya mountain.

39.s:
rathaiḥ pañcāpi tattīrthaṃ saṃprāptāste narottamāḥ /
maghyāhnamaye prītāḥ saptagodāvaraṃ jalam //
39.d:
रथैः पञ्चापि तत्तीर्थं संप्राप्तास्ते नरोत्तमाः ।
मघ्याह्नमये प्रीताः सप्तगोदावरं जलम् ॥
39.m: Those best of men also, with their chariots, reached that tīrtha; / having reached the water of Saptagodāvara at midday, pleased,

39.s:
prāpya viśrāmahetvarthamavaterustvarānvitāḥ /
teṣāṃ sārathayaścāśvān snātvā pītodakāplutān //
39.d:
प्राप्य विश्रामहेत्वर्थमवतेरुस्त्वरान्विताः ।
तेषां सारथयश्चाश्वान् स्नात्वा पीतोदकाप्लुतान् ॥
39.m: they stepped down with haste for the purpose of resting. / And their charioteers, having bathed the horses and refreshed them with water to drink,

39.s:
ramaṇīye vanoddeśe pracārārthe samutsṛjan /
śāḍhvalāḍhyeṣu deśeṣu muhurttādeva vājinaḥ //
39.d:
रमणीये वनोद्देशे प्रचारार्थे समुत्सृजन् ।
शाढ्वलाढ्येषु देशेषु मुहुर्त्तादेव वाजिनः ॥
39.m: released them in a delightful woodland region to graze. / In places rich in lush grass, within a mere moment the horses,

39.s:
tṛptāḥ samādravan sarve devāyatanamuttamam /
turaṅgakhuranirghoṣaṃ śrutvā tā yoṣitāṃ varāḥ //
39.d:
तृप्ताः समाद्रवन् सर्वे देवायतनमुत्तमम् ।
तुरङ्गखुरनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा ता योषितां वराः ॥
39.m: being satisfied, all ran toward the excellent abode of the deity. / Hearing the noise of the horses' hooves, those best of women,

39.s:
kimetaditi coktvaiva prajagmurhāṭakeśvaram /
āruhya balabhīṃ tāstu samudaikṣanta sarvaśaḥ //
39.d:
किमेतदिति चोक्त्वैव प्रजग्मुर्हाटकेश्वरम् ।
आरुह्य बलभीं तास्तु समुदैक्षन्त सर्वशः ॥
39.m: saying, "What is this?", went straight to Hāṭakeśvara. / Mounting the upper terrace, they gazed all around.

39.s:
apaśyaṃstīrthasalile snāyamānān narottamān /
tataścitrāṅgadā dṛṣṭvā jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam/ /
surathaṃ hasatī prāha saṃrohatpulakā sakhīm //
39.d:
अपश्यंस्तीर्थसलिले स्नायमानान् नरोत्तमान् ।
ततश्चित्राङ्गदा दृष्ट्वा जटामण्डलधारिणम्। ।
सुरथं हसती प्राह संरोहत्पुलका सखीम् ॥
39.m: They saw the best of men bathing in the water of the tīrtha. / Then Citrāṅgadā, having seen Suratha wearing a circle of matted hair, / laughing, with horripilation rising, said to her companion:

39.s:
yo 'sau yuvā nīlaghanaprakāśaḥ saṃdṛśyate dīrghabhujaḥ sūrūpaḥ /
sa eva nūnaṃ naradevasūnurvṛto mayā pūrvataraṃ patiryaḥ //
39.d:
यो ऽसौ युवा नीलघनप्रकाशः संदृश्यते दीर्घभुजः सूरूपः ।
स एव नूनं नरदेवसूनुर्वृतो मया पूर्वतरं पतिर्यः ॥
39.m: "That youth who is seen, shining like a dark cloud, long-armed and handsome, / he indeed is the son of the king who was chosen by me earlier as my husband.

39.s:
yaścaiva jāmbūvanadatulyavarṇaḥ śvetaṃ jaṭābhāramadhārayiṣyat /
sa eṣa nūnaṃ tapatāṃ variṣṭho ṛtadhvajo nātra vicāramasti //
39.d:
यश्चैव जाम्बूवनदतुल्यवर्णः श्वेतं जटाभारमधारयिष्यत् ।
स एष नूनं तपतां वरिष्ठो ऋतध्वजो नात्र विचारमस्ति ॥
39.m: And he who has the color of Jāmbūnada gold and wears a white mass of matted hair, / he indeed is Ṛtadhvaja, the best among ascetics; there is no doubt about this.

39.s:
tato 'bravīdatho hṛṣṭā nandayantī sakhījanam /
eṣo 'paro 'syaiva suto jāvālirnātra saṃśayaḥ //
39.d:
ततो ऽब्रवीदथो हृष्टा नन्दयन्ती सखीजनम् ।
एषो ऽपरो ऽस्यैव सुतो जावालिर्नात्र संशयः ॥
39.m: Then, delighted, gladdening her companions, she said: / "This other one is his son Jābāli; there is no doubt about it."

39.s:
ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ balabhyā avatīrya ca /
samāsatāgrataḥ śaṃbhorgāyantyo gītikāṃ śubhām //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं बलभ्या अवतीर्य च ।
समासताग्रतः शंभोर्गायन्त्यो गीतिकां शुभाम् ॥
39.m: Having spoken these words and descended from the terrace, / they sat before Śambhu, singing an auspicious song:

39.s:
namo 'stu śarva śaṃbo trinetra cārugātra trailokyanātha umāpate dakṣayajñavidhvaṃsakara kāmāhganāsana ghora pāpapraṇāśana mahāpuruṣa mahogramūrte sarvasattvakṣayaṅkara śubhaṅkara maheśvara triśūladhārin smarāre guhāvāsin digvāsaḥ mahāśaṅkaśekhara (5) jaṭādhara kapālamālāvibhūṣikaśarīra vāmacakṣuḥ bāmadeva prajādhyakṣa bhagākṣṇoḥ kṣayaṅkara bhīmasena mahāsenanātha paśupate kāmāṅgadahana catvaravāsin śiva mahādeva īśāna saṃkara bhīma bhava vaṣabhadhvaja jaṭila prauḍha mahānāṭyeśvara bhūriratna (10) avimuktaka rudraśvara sthāṇo ekaliṅga kālindīpriya śrīkaṇṭha nīlakaṇṭha aparājita ripubhayaṅkara saṃtoṣapate vāmadeva aghora tatpuruṣa mahāghora aghoramūrtta śānta sarasvatīkānta kīnāṭa sahasramūrtte mahodbhava (15) vibo kālāgnirudra hara mahīdharapriya sarvatīrthādhivāsa haṃsa kāmeśvara kedārādhipate paripūrṇa mucukunda madhunivāsin kṛpāṇapāṇe bhayaṅkara vidyārāja somarāja kāmarāja uñjaka añjanarājakanyāhṛdacalavasate samudraśāyin (20) gajamukha ghaṇṭeśvara gokarṇa brahmayone sahasravaktrākṣicaraṇa hāṭakeśvara namo 'stu te /
etasminnantare prāptāḥ sarva evarṣipārthivāḥ /
draṣṭuṃ trailokyakartāraṃ tryambakaṃ hāṭakeśvaram //
39.d:
नमो ऽस्तु शर्व शंबो त्रिनेत्र चारुगात्र त्रैलोक्यनाथ उमापते दक्षयज्ञविध्वंसकर कामाह्गनासन घोर पापप्रणाशन महापुरुष महोग्रमूर्ते सर्वसत्त्वक्षयङ्कर शुभङ्कर महेश्वर त्रिशूलधारिन् स्मरारे गुहावासिन् दिग्वासः महाशङ्कशेखर (5) जटाधर कपालमालाविभूषिकशरीर वामचक्षुः बामदेव प्रजाध्यक्ष भगाक्ष्णोः क्षयङ्कर भीमसेन महासेननाथ पशुपते कामाङ्गदहन चत्वरवासिन् शिव महादेव ईशान संकर भीम भव वषभध्वज जटिल प्रौढ महानाट्येश्वर भूरिरत्न (10) अविमुक्तक रुद्रश्वर स्थाणो एकलिङ्ग कालिन्दीप्रिय श्रीकण्ठ नीलकण्ठ अपराजित रिपुभयङ्कर संतोषपते वामदेव अघोर तत्पुरुष महाघोर अघोरमूर्त्त शान्त सरस्वतीकान्त कीनाट सहस्रमूर्त्ते महोद्भव (15) विबो कालाग्निरुद्र हर महीधरप्रिय सर्वतीर्थाधिवास हंस कामेश्वर केदाराधिपते परिपूर्ण मुचुकुन्द मधुनिवासिन् कृपाणपाणे भयङ्कर विद्याराज सोमराज कामराज उञ्जक अञ्जनराजकन्याहृदचलवसते समुद्रशायिन् (20) गजमुख घण्टेश्वर गोकर्ण ब्रह्मयोने सहस्रवक्त्राक्षिचरण हाटकेश्वर नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्राप्ताः सर्व एवर्षिपार्थिवाः ।
द्रष्टुं त्रैलोक्यकर्तारं त्र्यम्बकं हाटकेश्वरम् ॥
39.m: "Homage to you, O Śarva, Śambhu, three-eyed one, of handsome limbs, lord of the three worlds, husband of Umā, destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, destroyer of the body of Kāma, terrible one, destroyer of sins, supreme person, of immensely fierce form, destroyer of all beings, auspicious one, Maheśvara, wielder of the trident, enemy of Smara, cave-dweller, sky-clad one, crowned with the great conch, / wearer of matted hair, whose body is adorned with a garland of skulls, left-eyed one, Vāmadeva, overseer of creatures, destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga, Bhīmasena, lord of Mahāsena, Paśupati, burner of the limbs of Kāma, dweller in crossroads, Śiva, Mahādeva, Īśāna, Śaṅkara, Bhīma, Bhava, bull-bannered one, matted-haired one, mature one, lord of the great dance, possessor of abundant gems, / Avimuktaka, Rudreśvara, Sthāṇu, Ekaliṅga, lover of the Kālindī, Śrīkaṇṭha, Nīlakaṇṭha, unconquered one, terrifier of enemies, lord of contentment, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, exceedingly terrible one, of non-terrific form, peaceful one, beloved of Sarasvatī, Kīnāṭa, having a thousand forms, of great origin, / omnipresent one, Kālāgnirudra, Hara, lover of the mountain, residing in all tīrthas, Haṃsa, lord of love, lord of Kedāra, complete one, Mucukunda, dweller in Madhu, sword in hand, frightful one, king of knowledge, king of the moon, king of desire, Uñjaka, whose abode is in the heart of the daughter of the king of Añjana, sleeper upon the ocean, / elephant-faced one, Ghaṇṭeśvara, Gokarṇa, source of Brahmā, having a thousand faces, eyes, and feet, Hāṭakeśvara, homage be to you!" / In the meantime, all those sages and kings arrived / to see Hāṭakeśvara, the three-eyed creator of the three worlds.

39.s:
samārūḍhāśca susnātā dadṛśuryoṣitaśca tāḥ /
sthitāstu puratastasya gāyantyo geyamuttamam //
39.d:
समारूढाश्च सुस्नाता ददृशुर्योषितश्च ताः ।
स्थितास्तु पुरतस्तस्य गायन्त्यो गेयमुत्तमम् ॥
39.m: Having bathed well and ascended, they saw those women / standing before him, singing an excellent song.

39.s:
tataḥ sudevatanayo viśvakarmasutāṃ priyām /
dṛṣṭvā hṛṣitacittastu saṃrohatpulako babhau //
39.d:
ततः सुदेवतनयो विश्वकर्मसुतां प्रियाम् ।
दृष्ट्वा हृषितचित्तस्तु संरोहत्पुलको बभौ ॥
39.m: Then the son of Sudeva, having seen his beloved, the daughter of Viśvakarman, / with an exhilarated heart, shone with horripilation rising.

39.s:
ṛtadhvajo 'pi tanvaṅgīṃ dṛṣṭvā citrāṅgadāṃ sthitām /
pratyabhijñāya yogātmā babhau muditamānasaḥ //
39.d:
ऋतध्वजो ऽपि तन्वङ्गीं दृष्ट्वा चित्राङ्गदां स्थिताम् ।
प्रत्यभिज्ञाय योगात्मा बभौ मुदितमानसः ॥
39.m: Ṛtadhvaja too, the yogic soul, having seen the slender-limbed Citrāṅgadā standing / and recognized her, shone with a joyful mind.

39.s:
tatastu sahasābhyetya deveśaṃ hāṭakeśvaram /
saṃpūjayantastryakṣaṃ te stuvantaḥ saṃsthitāḥ kramāt //
39.d:
ततस्तु सहसाभ्येत्य देवेशं हाटकेश्वरम् ।
संपूजयन्तस्त्र्यक्षं ते स्तुवन्तः संस्थिताः क्रमात् ॥
39.m: Then, coming hastily toward Hāṭakeśvara, the lord of gods, / worshipping and praising the three-eyed one, they stood in order.

39.s:
citrāṅgadāpi tān dṛṣṭvā ṛtadhvajapurogamān /
samaṃ tābhiḥ kṛsāṅgībhirabhyutthāyābhyavādayat //
39.d:
चित्राङ्गदापि तान् दृष्ट्वा ऋतध्वजपुरोगमान् ।
समं ताभिः कृसाङ्गीभिरभ्युत्थायाभ्यवादयत् ॥
39.m: Citrāṅgadā also, having seen them led by Ṛtadhvaja, / stood up together with those slender-limbed women and greeted them.

39.s:
sa ca tāḥ pratinandyaiva samaṃ putreṇa tāpasaḥ /
samaṃ nṛpatibhirhṛṣṭaḥ saṃviveśa yathāsukham //
39.d:
स च ताः प्रतिनन्द्यैव समं पुत्रेण तापसः ।
समं नृपतिभिर्हृष्टः संविवेश यथासुखम् ॥
39.m:
And the ascetic, having welcomed them together with his son,
sat down at ease, delighted, along with the kings.

39.s:
tataḥ kapivaraḥ prāpto ghṛtācyā saha sundari /
snātvā godāvarītīrthe didṛkṣurhāṭakeśvaram //
39.d:
ततः कपिवरः प्राप्तो घृताच्या सह सुन्दरि ।
स्नात्वा गोदावरीतीर्थे दिदृक्षुर्हाटकेश्वरम् ॥
39.m:
Then the excellent monkey arrived together with Ghṛtācī, O fair lady,
having bathed at the Godāvarī tīrtha, wishing to behold Hāṭakeśvara.

39.s:
tato 'paśyat sutāṃ tanvīṃ ghṛtācī śubhadarśanām /
sāpi tāṃ mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭābhūdvaravarṇinī //
39.d:
ततो ऽपश्यत् सुतां तन्वीं घृताची शुभदर्शनाम् ।
सापि तां मातरं दृष्ट्वा हृष्टाभूद्वरवर्णिनी ॥
39.m:
Then Ghṛtācī beheld her slender daughter of auspicious appearance,
and she too, the fair-complexioned one, was delighted on seeing her mother.

39.s:
tato ghṛtācī svāṃ putrīṃ pariṣvajya nyapīḍayat /
snehāt savāṣpanayanāṃ muhustāṃ parijighravīt //
39.d:
ततो घृताची स्वां पुत्रीं परिष्वज्य न्यपीडयत् ।
स्नेहात् सवाष्पनयनां मुहुस्तां परिजिघ्रवीत् ॥
39.m:
Then Ghṛtācī embraced her daughter and held her close;
out of affection, with tearful eyes, she kissed her head again and again.

39.s:
tato ṛtadhvajaḥ śrīmān kapiṃ vacanamabravīt /
gacchanetuṃ guhyakaṃ tvamañjanādrau mahāñjanam //
39.d:
ततो ऋतध्वजः श्रीमान् कपिं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
गच्छनेतुं गुह्यकं त्वमञ्जनाद्रौ महाञ्जनम् ॥
39.m:
Then the glorious Ṛtadhvaja said these words to the monkey:
'Go to bring the Guhyaka Mahāñjana on Mount Añjana,

39.s:
pātālādapi daityeśaṃ vīraṃ kandaramālinam /
svargād gandharvarājānaṃ parjanyaṃ śīghramānaya //
39.d:
पातालादपि दैत्येशं वीरं कन्दरमालिनम् ।
स्वर्गाद् गन्धर्वराजानं पर्जन्यं शीघ्रमानय ॥
39.m:
and also the heroic lord of the Daityas, Kandaramālin, from Pātāla;
quickly bring Parjanya, the king of the Gandharvas, from heaven.'

39.s:
ityevamukte muninā prāha devavatī kapim /
gālavaṃ vānaraśreṣṭha ihānetuṃ tvamarhasi //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्ते मुनिना प्राह देववती कपिम् ।
गालवं वानरश्रेष्ठ इहानेतुं त्वमर्हसि ॥
39.m:
When the sage had spoken thus, Devavatī said to the monkey:
'O best of monkeys, you ought to bring Gālava here.'

39.s:
ityevamukte vacane kapirmarutavikramaḥ /
gatvāñjanaṃ samāmantrya jagāmāmaraparvatam //
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने कपिर्मरुतविक्रमः ।
गत्वाञ्जनं समामन्त्र्य जगामामरपर्वतम् ॥
39.m:
When these words were spoken, the monkey, whose prowess was like the wind's,
went, invited Añjana, and proceeded to the mountain of the gods.

39.s:
parjanyaṃ tatra cāmantrya preṣayitvā mahāśrame /
saptagodāvare tīrthe pātālamagamat kapiḥ //
39.d:
पर्जन्यं तत्र चामन्त्र्य प्रेषयित्वा महाश्रमे ।
सप्तगोदावरे तीर्थे पातालमगमत् कपिः ॥
39.m:
Having invited Parjanya there and sent him to the great hermitage
at the Saptagodāvara tīrtha, the monkey went to Pātāla.

39.s:
tatrāmantrya mahāvīryaṃ kapiḥ kandaramālinam /
pātālādabhiniṣkramya mahīṃ paryacarajjavī //
39.d:
तत्रामन्त्र्य महावीर्यं कपिः कन्दरमालिनम् ।
पातालादभिनिष्क्रम्य महीं पर्यचरज्जवी ॥
39.m:
Having invited the mighty Kandaramālin there,
the swift monkey came out of Pātāla and roamed over the earth.

39.s:
gālaṃ tapaso yoniṃ dṛṣṭvā māhiṣmatīmanu /
samutpatyānayacchīghraṃ saptagodāvaraṃ jalam //
39.d:
गालं तपसो योनिं दृष्ट्वा माहिष्मतीमनु ।
समुत्पत्यानयच्छीघ्रं सप्तगोदावरं जलम् ॥
39.m:
Having seen Gālava, the source of ascetic power, near Māhiṣmatī,
he flew up and quickly brought him to the waters of Saptagodāvara.

39.s:
tatra snātvā vidhānena saṃprāpto hāṭakeśvaram /
dadṛśe nandayantī ca sthitāṃ devavatīmapi //
39.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा विधानेन संप्राप्तो हाटकेश्वरम् ।
ददृशे नन्दयन्ती च स्थितां देववतीमपि ॥
39.m:
Having bathed there according to rule, he reached Hāṭakeśvara;
and he saw Nandayantī, as well as Devavatī standing there.

39.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā gālavaṃ caiva samutthāyābhyavādayat /
sa cārciṣyanmahādevaṃ maharṣīnabhyavādayat /
te cāpi nṛpatiśreṣṭhastaṃ saṃpūjya tapodhanam //
39.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा गालवं चैव समुत्थायाभ्यवादयत् ।
स चार्चिष्यन्महादेवं महर्षीनभ्यवादयत् ।
ते चापि नृपतिश्रेष्ठस्तं संपूज्य तपोधनम् ॥

39.s:
praharṣamatulaṃ gatvā upaviṣṭā yathāsukham /
teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu tadā vānaropanimantritāḥ //
39.d:
प्रहर्षमतुलं गत्वा उपविष्टा यथासुखम् ।
तेषूपविष्टेषु तदा वानरोपनिमन्त्रिताः ॥
39.m:
Having attained matchless joy, they sat down at ease.
When they were seated, the high-souled Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and Dānavas,

39.s:
samāyātā mahātmāno yakṣagandharvadānavāḥ /
tānāgatān samīkṣyaiva putryastāḥ pṛthulocanāḥ //
39.d:
समायाता महात्मानो यक्षगन्धर्वदानवाः ।
तानागतान् समीक्ष्यैव पुत्र्यस्ताः पृथुलोचनाः ॥
39.m:
invited by the monkey, arrived.
Beholding them arrived, those large-eyed daughters,

39.s:
snehārdranayanāḥ sarvāstadā sasvajire pitṝn /
nandayantyādikā dṛṣṭvā sapitṛkā varānanā //
39.d:
स्नेहार्द्रनयनाः सर्वास्तदा सस्वजिरे पितॄन् ।
नन्दयन्त्यादिका दृष्ट्वा सपितृका वरानना ॥
39.m:
all with eyes moist with affection, then embraced their fathers.
Seeing Nandayantī and the others united with their fathers, the fair-faced

39.s:
savāṣpanayanā jātā viśvakarmasutā tadā /
atha tāmāha sa muniḥ satyaṃ satyadhvajo vacaḥ //
39.d:
सवाष्पनयना जाता विश्वकर्मसुता तदा ।
अथ तामाह स मुनिः सत्यं सत्यध्वजो वचः ॥
39.m:
daughter of Viśvakarman then became tearful-eyed.
Then the sage Satyadhvaja spoke these true words to her:

39.s:
mā viṣādaṃ kṛtāḥ putri pitāyaṃ tava vānaraḥ /
sā tadvacanamākarṇya vrīḍopahatacetanā //
39.d:
मा विषादं कृताः पुत्रि पितायं तव वानरः ।
सा तद्वचनमाकर्ण्य व्रीडोपहतचेतना ॥
39.m:
'Do not grieve, daughter; this monkey is your father.'
Hearing his words, her mind was struck with shame:

39.s:
kathaṃ tu viśvakarmāsau vānaratvaṃ gato 'dhunā /
duṣputryāṃ mayijātāyaṃ tasmāt tyakṣe kalevaram //
39.d:
कथं तु विश्वकर्मासौ वानरत्वं गतो ऽधुना ।
दुष्पुत्र्यां मयिजातायं तस्मात् त्यक्षे कलेवरम् ॥
39.m:
'How has this Viśvakarman now fallen into the state of a monkey
because I was born a wicked daughter? Therefore I shall abandon my body!'

39.s:
iti saṃcintya manasā ṛtadhvajamuvāca ha /
paritrāyasva māṃ brahman pāpopahatacetanām //
39.d:
इति संचिन्त्य मनसा ऋतध्वजमुवाच ह ।
परित्रायस्व मां ब्रह्मन् पापोपहतचेतनाम् ॥
39.m:
Reflecting thus in her mind, she spoke to Ṛtadhvaja:
'Protect me, O Brahmin, whose mind is afflicted by sin!

39.s:
pitṛghnī martumicchāmi tadanujñātumarhasi /
athovāca munistanvīṃ mā viṣādaṃ kṛthādhunā //
39.d:
पितृघ्नी मर्तुमिच्छामि तदनुज्ञातुमर्हसि ।
अथोवाच मुनिस्तन्वीं मा विषादं कृथाधुना ॥
39.m:
I, a slayer of my father, wish to die; you ought to permit it.'
Then the sage said to the slender lady: 'Do not grieve now!

39.s:
bhāvyasya naiva nāśo 'sti nanmā tyākṣīḥ kalevaram /
bhaviṣyati pitā tubhyaṃ bhuyayo 'pyamaravarddhakiḥ //
39.d:
भाव्यस्य नैव नाशो ऽस्ति नन्मा त्याक्षीः कलेवरम् ।
भविष्यति पिता तुभ्यं भुययो ऽप्यमरवर्द्धकिः ॥
39.m:
What is destined to be cannot be destroyed; so do not cast off your body.
Your father will once again become the architect of the gods.

39.s:
jāte 'patye ghṛtācyāṃ tu nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
ityevamukte vacane muninā bhāvitātmanā //
39.d:
जाते ऽपत्ये घृताच्यां तु नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने मुनिना भावितात्मना ॥
39.m:
When a child is born to Ghṛtācī, no doubt should be entertained here.'
When these words were spoken by the sage whose soul was refined,

39.s:
ghṛtācī tāṃ sambhyetya prāha citrāṅgadāṃ vacaḥ /
putri tyajasva śokaṃ tvaṃ māsaurdaśabhirātmajaḥ //
39.d:
घृताची तां सम्भ्येत्य प्राह चित्राङ्गदां वचः ।
पुत्रि त्यजस्व शोकं त्वं मासौर्दशभिरात्मजः ॥
39.m:
Ghṛtācī approached Citrāṅgadā and said these words to her:
'Daughter, cast away your grief; in ten months a son

39.s:
bhaviṣyati putustubhyaṃ matsakāśānna saṃśayaḥ /
ityevamuktā saṃhṛṣṭā babhau citrāṅgadā tadā //
39.d:
भविष्यति पुतुस्तुभ्यं मत्सकाशान्न संशयः ।
इत्येवमुक्ता संहृष्टा बभौ चित्राङ्गदा तदा ॥
39.m:
will be born to your father from me, without a doubt.'
Addressed thus, Citrāṅgadā then shone forth, delighted,

39.s:
pratīkṣantī sucārvaṅgī vivāhe pitṛdarśanam /
sarvāstā api tāvantaṃ kālaṃ sutanukanyakāḥ //
39.d:
प्रतीक्षन्ती सुचार्वङ्गी विवाहे पितृदर्शनम् ।
सर्वास्ता अपि तावन्तं कालं सुतनुकन्यकाः ॥
39.m:
the exceedingly fair-limbed lady waiting to see her father at her wedding.
All those lovely-bodied maidens also, for that length of time,

39.s:
pratyaikṣanta vivāhaṃ hi tasyā eva priyepsayā /
tato daśasu māseṣu samatīteṣvathāpsarāḥ //
39.d:
प्रत्यैक्षन्त विवाहं हि तस्या एव प्रियेप्सया ।
ततो दशसु मासेषु समतीतेष्वथाप्सराः ॥
39.m:
awaited the marriage out of a desire to please her alone.
Then, when ten months had elapsed, the apsaras

39.s:
tasmn godāvarītīrthe prasūtā tanayaṃ nalam /
jāte 'patye kapitvācca viśvakarmāpyamucyata //
39.d:
तस्म्न् गोदावरीतीर्थे प्रसूता तनयं नलम् ।
जाते ऽपत्ये कपित्वाच्च विश्वकर्माप्यमुच्यत ॥
39.m:
gave birth to a son, Nala, at that Godāvarī tīrtha.
When the child was born, Viśvakarman was freed from monkeyhood.

39.s:
samabhyetya priyāṃ putrīṃ paryaṣvajata cādarāt /
tataḥ prītena manasā sasmāra suravarddhakiḥ //
39.d:
समभ्येत्य प्रियां पुत्रीं पर्यष्वजत चादरात् ।
ततः प्रीतेन मनसा सस्मार सुरवर्द्धकिः ॥
39.m:
Approaching his dear daughter, he embraced her with affection.
Then, with a pleased mind, the architect of the gods remembered

39.s:
surāṇāmadhipaṃ śakraṃ sahaiva surakinnaraiḥ /
tvaṣṭrātha saṃsmṛtaḥ śakro marudgaṇavṛtastadā //
39.d:
सुराणामधिपं शक्रं सहैव सुरकिन्नरैः ।
त्वष्ट्राथ संस्मृतः शक्रो मरुद्गणवृतस्तदा ॥
39.m:
Śakra, the lord of the gods, together with the gods and Kinnaras.
Remembered by Tvaṣṭṛ, Śakra, surrounded by the host of the Maruts,

39.s:
suraiḥ sarudraiḥ saṃprāptastattīrtha hāṭakāhvayam /
samāyāteṣu deveṣu gandharveṣvapsarassu ca //
39.d:
सुरैः सरुद्रैः संप्राप्तस्तत्तीर्थ हाटकाह्वयम् ।
समायातेषु देवेषु गन्धर्वेष्वप्सरस्सु च ॥
39.m:
arrived at that tīrtha named Hāṭaka, along with the gods and Rudras.
When the gods, Gandharvas, and apsarases had gathered,

39.s:
indradyumno muniśreṣṭhamṛtadhvajamuvāca ha /
jābālerdīyatāṃ brahman sutākandaramālinaḥ //
39.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नो मुनिश्रेष्ठमृतध्वजमुवाच ह ।
जाबालेर्दीयतां ब्रह्मन् सुताकन्दरमालिनः ॥
39.m:
Indradyumna spoke to the best of sages, Ṛtadhvaja:
'O Brahmin, let the daughter of Kandaramālin be given to Jābāli;

39.s:
gṛhṇātu vidhivat pāṇiṃ daiteyyāstanayastava /
nandayantīṃ ca śakuniḥ pariṇetuṃ svarūpavān //
39.d:
गृह्णातु विधिवत् पाणिं दैतेय्यास्तनयस्तव ।
नन्दयन्तीं च शकुनिः परिणेतुं स्वरूपवान् ॥
39.m:
let your son take the hand of the Daitya woman according to rule;
and let the handsome Śakuni marry Nandayantī;

39.s:
mameyaṃ vedavatyastu tvāṣṭroyī surathasya ca /
bāḍhamityabravīddhṛṣṭo munirmanusutaṃ nṛpam //
39.d:
ममेयं वेदवत्यस्तु त्वाष्ट्रोयी सुरथस्य च ।
बाढमित्यब्रवीद्धृष्टो मुनिर्मनुसुतं नृपम् ॥
39.m:
let this Vedavatī be mine, and the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ be Suratha's.'
'So be it,' said the delighted sage to the king, the son of Manu.

39.s:
tato 'nucakruḥ saṃhṛṣṭā vivāhavidhimuttamam /
ṛtvijo 'bhūd gālavastu hutvā havyaṃ vidhanataḥ //
39.d:
ततो ऽनुचक्रुः संहृष्टा विवाहविधिमुत्तमम् ।
ऋत्विजो ऽभूद् गालवस्तु हुत्वा हव्यं विधनतः ॥
39.m:
Then, delighted, they performed the excellent rites of marriage.
Gālava became the officiating priest, offering the oblation according to rule.

39.s:
gāyante tatra gandharvā nṛtyante 'psarasastathā /
ādau jābālinaḥ pāṇirgṛhīto daityakanyayā //
39.d:
गायन्ते तत्र गन्धर्वा नृत्यन्ते ऽप्सरसस्तथा ।
आदौ जाबालिनः पाणिर्गृहीतो दैत्यकन्यया ॥
39.m:
There the Gandharvas sang and the apsarases danced.
First, the hand of the Daitya maiden was taken by Jābāli;

39.s:
indradyumnena tadanu vedavatyā vidhānataḥ /
tataḥ śakuninā pāṇirgṛhīto yakṣakanyayā //
39.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नेन तदनु वेदवत्या विधानतः ।
ततः शकुनिना पाणिर्गृहीतो यक्षकन्यया ॥
39.m:
after that, the hand of Vedavatī was taken by Indradyumna according to rule;
then the hand of the Yakṣa maiden was taken by Śakuni;

39.s:
citrāṅgadāyāḥ kalyāṇi surathaḥ pāṇimagrahīt /
evaṃ kramād vivāhastu nirvṛttastanumadhyame //
39.d:
चित्राङ्गदायाः कल्याणि सुरथः पाणिमग्रहीत् ।
एवं क्रमाद् विवाहस्तु निर्वृत्तस्तनुमध्यमे ॥
39.m:
Suratha took the hand of Citrāṅgadā, O auspicious one.
Thus in order the marriage was completed, O slender-waisted lady.

39.s:
vṛtte munirvivāhe tu śakrādīn prāha daivatān /
asmistīrthe bhavadbhistu saptagodāvare sadā //
39.d:
वृत्ते मुनिर्विवाहे तु शक्रादीन् प्राह दैवतान् ।
अस्मिस्तीर्थे भवद्भिस्तु सप्तगोदावरे सदा ॥
39.m:
When the wedding was completed, the sage said to the deities headed by Śakra:
'You should always stay at this Saptagodāvara tīrtha,

39.s:
stheyaṃ viśeṣato māsamimaṃ mādhavamuttamam /
bāḍhamuktvā surāḥ sarve jagmurhṛṣṭā divaṃ kramāt //
39.d:
स्थेयं विशेषतो मासमिमं माधवमुत्तमम् ।
बाढमुक्त्वा सुराः सर्वे जग्मुर्हृष्टा दिवं क्रमात् ॥
39.m:
especially during this excellent month of Mādhava.'
Saying 'So be it,' all the gods, delighted, went to heaven in succession.

39.s:
munayo munimādāya saputraṃ jagmurādarāt /
bhāryāścādāya rājānaḥ svaṃ svaṃ nagaramāgatāḥ //
39.d:
मुनयो मुनिमादाय सपुत्रं जग्मुरादरात् ।
भार्याश्चादाय राजानः स्वं स्वं नगरमागताः ॥
39.m:
The sages, taking the sage along with his son, went with respect;
and taking their wives, the kings returned each to his own city.

39.s:
prahṛṣṭāḥ sukhinastasthuḥ bhuñjate viṣayān priyān /
citrāṅgadāyāḥ kalyāṇi evaṃ vṛttaṃ purā kila /
tanmāṃ kamalapatrākṣi bhajasva lalanottame //
39.d:
प्रहृष्टाः सुखिनस्तस्थुः भुञ्जते विषयान् प्रियान् ।
चित्राङ्गदायाः कल्याणि एवं वृत्तं पुरा किल ।
तन्मां कमलपत्राक्षि भजस्व ललनोत्तमे ॥

39.s:
ityevamuktvā naradevasūnustāṃ bhūmidevasya sutāṃ varorum /
stuvanmṛgākṣīṃ mṛdunā krameṇa sā cāpi vākyaṃ nṛpatiṃ babhāṣe //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ekonacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
39.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा नरदेवसूनुस्तां भूमिदेवस्य सुतां वरोरुम् ।
स्तुवन्मृगाक्षीं मृदुना क्रमेण सा चापि वाक्यं नृपतिं बभाषे ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे एकोनचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
39.m:
Having spoken thus to the fair-thighed daughter of the Brahmin, / praising that deer-eyed maiden with gentle words, the king's son paused; and she addressed the king in turn:

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter in the holy Vāmana Purāṇa.

40.s:
arajā uvāca /
nātmānaṃ tava dāsyāmi buhanoktena kiṃ tava /
rakṣantī bhavataḥ śāpādātmānaṃ ca mahī pate //
40.d:
अरजा उवाच ।
नात्मानं तव दास्यामि बुहनोक्तेन किं तव ।
रक्षन्ती भवतः शापादात्मानं च मही पते ॥
40.m: Arajā said: / 'I shall not surrender myself to you; what need is there of many words from you? / I am protecting myself, and you, O lord of the earth, from a curse.'

40.s:
prahlāda uvāca/ /
itthaṃ vivadamānāṃ tāṃ bhārgavendrasutāṃ balāt /
kāmopahatacittātmā vyadhvaṃsayata mandadhīḥ //
40.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच। ।
इत्थं विवदमानां तां भार्गवेन्द्रसुतां बलात् ।
कामोपहतचित्तात्मा व्यध्वंसयत मन्दधीः ॥
40.m: Prahlāda said: / 'Though that daughter of the chief of Bhārgavas was arguing in this way, / the dull-witted king, his heart and mind overwhelmed by lust, violated her by force.

40.s:
tāṃ kṛtvā cyutacāpitrāṃ madāndhaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
niścakrāmāśramāt tasmād gataśca nagaraṃ nijam //
40.d:
तां कृत्वा च्युतचापित्रां मदान्धः पृथिवीपतिः ।
निश्चक्रामाश्रमात् तस्माद् गतश्च नगरं निजम् ॥
40.m: Having brought about her fall from purity, the ruler of the earth, blind with passion, / departed from that hermitage and went to his own city.

40.s:
sāpi śukrasutā tanvī arajā rajasāplutā /
āśramādatha niragatya bahistasthāvadhosukhī //
40.d:
सापि शुक्रसुता तन्वी अरजा रजसाप्लुता ।
आश्रमादथ निरगत्य बहिस्तस्थावधोसुखी ॥
40.m: That slender daughter of Śukra, Arajā, covered in dust, / then stepped out of the hermitage and stood outside, her face turned downwards.

40.s:
cintayantī svapitaraṃ rudatī ca muhurmuhuḥ /
mahāgrahopatapteva rohiṇī śaśinaḥ priyā //
40.d:
चिन्तयन्ती स्वपितरं रुदती च मुहुर्मुहुः ।
महाग्रहोपतप्तेव रोहिणी शशिनः प्रिया ॥
40.m: Brooding upon her father and weeping again and again, / she seemed like Rohiṇī, the beloved of the moon, afflicted by a mighty planet.

40.s:
tato bahutithe kāle samāpte yajñakarmaṇi /
pātālādāgamacchukraḥ khamāśramapadaṃ muniḥ //
40.d:
ततो बहुतिथे काले समाप्ते यज्ञकर्मणि ।
पातालादागमच्छुक्रः खमाश्रमपदं मुनिः ॥
40.m: Then after a long time, when the sacrificial rite was completed, / the sage Śukra returned through the sky to the hermitage grounds from Pātāla.

40.s:
āśramānte ca dadṛśe sutāṃ daitya rajakhalām /
meghalekhāmivākāśe saṃdhyārāgeṇa rañjitām //
40.d:
आश्रमान्ते च ददृशे सुतां दैत्य रजखलाम् ।
मेघलेखामिवाकाशे संध्यारागेण रञ्जिताम् ॥
40.m: And at the edge of the hermitage, O Daitya, he saw his daughter in her menstrual course, / like a streak of cloud in the sky colored by the twilight glow.

40.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paripapraccha putri kenāsi dharṣitā /
kaḥ krīḍati saroṣeṇa samamāśīviṣeṇa hi //
40.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा परिपप्रच्छ पुत्रि केनासि धर्षिता ।
कः क्रीडति सरोषेण सममाशीविषेण हि ॥
40.m: Seeing her, he asked: "Daughter, by whom have you been violated? / Who plays with an enraged venomous serpent?

40.s:
ko 'dyaiva yāmyāṃ nagarīṃ gamiṣyati sudurmatiḥ /
yastvāṃ suddhasamācārāṃ vidhvaṃsayati pāpakṛt //
40.d:
को ऽद्यैव याम्यां नगरीं गमिष्यति सुदुर्मतिः ।
यस्त्वां सुद्धसमाचारां विध्वंसयति पापकृत् ॥
40.m: Who is that fool who will go to the city of Yama this very day, / that evil-doer who has ruined you of pure conduct?"

40.s:
tataḥ svapitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kampamānā punaḥ punāḥ /
rudantī vrīḍayopetā mandaṃ mandamuvāca ha //
40.d:
ततः स्वपितरं दृष्ट्वा कम्पमाना पुनः पुनाः ।
रुदन्ती व्रीडयोपेता मन्दं मन्दमुवाच ह ॥
40.m: Then, seeing her father, trembling again and again, / weeping and filled with shame, she spoke very slowly:

40.s:
tava śiṣyeṇa daṇḍena vāryamāṇena cāsakṛt /
balādanāthā rudatī nītāhaṃ vacanīyatām //
40.d:
तव शिष्येण दण्डेन वार्यमाणेन चासकृत् ।
बलादनाथा रुदती नीताहं वचनीयताम् ॥
40.m: "Though repeatedly restrained by me, by your pupil Daṇḍa / I, helpless and weeping, have been forcibly brought to reproach."

40.s:
etat putryā vacaḥ śrutvā krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ /
upaspṛśya śucirbhūtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt //
40.d:
एतत् पुत्र्या वचः श्रुत्वा क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ।
उपस्पृश्य शुचिर्भूत्वा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
40.m: Hearing these words of his daughter, his eyes reddened with rage; / having sipped water and become purified, he uttered these words:

40.s:
yasmāt tenāvinitena matto hyabhayamuttamam /
gauravaṃ ca tiraskṛtya cyutadharmārajā kṛtā //
40.d:
यस्मात् तेनाविनितेन मत्तो ह्यभयमुत्तमम् ।
गौरवं च तिरस्कृत्य च्युतधर्मारजा कृता ॥
40.m: "Since by that undisciplined one, disregarding the supreme protection / and respect due from me, Arajā was deprived of her virtue,

40.s:
tasmāt sarāṣṭraḥ sabalaḥ sabhṛtyo vāhanaiḥ saha /
saptarātrāntarād bhasma grāvavṛṣṭyā bhaviṣyati //
40.d:
तस्मात् सराष्ट्रः सबलः सभृत्यो वाहनैः सह ।
सप्तरात्रान्तराद् भस्म ग्राववृष्ट्या भविष्यति ॥
40.m: therefore together with his realm, his army, his servants and his mounts, / within seven nights he will become ashes through a shower of stones."

40.s:
ityevamuktvā munipuṅgavo 'sau śaptvā sa daṇḍaṃ svasutāmuvāca /
tvaṃ pāpamokṣārthamihaiva putri tiṣṭhasva kalyāṇi tapaścarantī //
40.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा मुनिपुङ्गवो ऽसौ शप्त्वा स दण्डं स्वसुतामुवाच ।
त्वं पापमोक्षार्थमिहैव पुत्रि तिष्ठस्व कल्याणि तपश्चरन्ती ॥
40.m: Having spoken thus, that foremost of sages cursed Daṇḍa and said to his daughter: / "For the sake of freeing yourself from sin, remain right here, O auspicious one, practicing austerities."

40.s:
śpatvetthaṃ bhagavān śukro daṇḍamikṣvākunandanam /
jagāma śiṣyasahitaḥ pātālaṃ dānavālayam //
40.d:
श्पत्वेत्थं भगवान् शुक्रो दण्डमिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनम् ।
जगाम शिष्यसहितः पातालं दानवालयम् ॥
40.m: Having thus cursed Daṇḍa, the son of Ikṣvāku, the venerable Śukra / went along with his disciples to Pātāla, the abode of the Dānavas.

40.s:
daṇḍo 'pi bhasmasād bhūtaḥ sarāṣṭrabalavāhanaḥ /
mahatā grāvavaraṣeṇa saptarātrāntare tadā //
40.d:
दण्डो ऽपि भस्मसाद् भूतः सराष्ट्रबलवाहनः ।
महता ग्राववरषेण सप्तरात्रान्तरे तदा ॥
40.m: And Daṇḍa too was reduced to ashes along with his kingdom, army, and mounts / by a great rain of stones within seven nights at that time.

40.s:
evaṃ tadṛṇḍakāraṇyaṃ parityajyanati devatā /
ālayaṃ rākṣasānāṃ tu kṛtaṃ devena śaṃbhunā //
40.d:
एवं तदृण्डकारण्यं परित्यज्यनति देवता ।
आलयं राक्षसानां तु कृतं देवेन शंभुना ॥
40.m: Thus that Daṇḍaka forest was abandoned by the deities, / but made an abode of the Rākṣasas by the god Śambhu.

40.s:
evaṃ parakalatrāṇi nayanti sukṛtīnapi /
bhasmabhūtān prākṛtāṃstu mahāntaṃ ca parābhavam //
40.d:
एवं परकलत्राणि नयन्ति सुकृतीनपि ।
भस्मभूतान् प्राकृतांस्तु महान्तं च पराभवम् ॥
40.m: In this manner the wives of others bring even the virtuous to ruin, / turning ordinary people to ashes and bringing them to utter defeat.

40.s:
tasmādandhaka durbuddhirna kāryā bhavatā tviyam /
prākṛtāpi dahennārī kimutāhodrinandinī //
40.d:
तस्मादन्धक दुर्बुद्धिर्न कार्या भवता त्वियम् ।
प्राकृतापि दहेन्नारी किमुताहोद्रिनन्दिनी ॥
40.m: Therefore, O Andhaka, you should not hold such an evil intent; / even an ordinary woman could burn [you], how much more the Daughter of the Mountain?

40.s:
śaṅkaro 'pi na daityeśa śakyo jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ /
draṣṭumapyamitaujaskaḥ kimu yodhayituṃ raṇe //
40.d:
शङ्करो ऽपि न दैत्येश शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः ।
द्रष्टुमप्यमितौजस्कः किमु योधयितुं रणे ॥
40.m: Śaṅkara too, O lord of the Daityas, cannot be conquered by the gods or asuras; / he of immeasurable splendor cannot even be looked upon, how much less fought in battle!"

40.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamukte vacane kruddhastāmrekṣaṇaḥ śvasan /
vākyamāha mahātejāḥ prahlādaṃ cāndhakāsuraḥ //
40.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने क्रुद्धस्ताम्रेक्षणः श्वसन् ।
वाक्यमाह महातेजाः प्रह्लादं चान्धकासुरः ॥
40.m: Pulastya said: / When these words were spoken, the mighty asura Andhaka, / enraged, breathing heavily, with copper-red eyes, said to Prahlāda:

40.s:
kiṃ mamāsau raṇe yoddhuṃ śaktastrimayano 'sura /
ekākī dharmarahito bhasmāruṇitavigrahaḥ //
40.d:
किं ममासौ रणे योद्धुं शक्तस्त्रिमयनो ऽसुर ।
एकाकी धर्मरहितो भस्मारुणितविग्रहः ॥
40.m: "Is that three-eyed one able to fight with me in battle, O asura— / [he who is] solitary, devoid of righteousness, his body reddened with ashes?

40.s:
nāndhako bibhiyādindrānnāmarebhyaḥ kathañcana /
sa kathaṃ vṛṣapatrākṣād bibheti strīmukhekṣakāt //
40.d:
नान्धको बिभियादिन्द्रान्नामरेभ्यः कथञ्चन ।
स कथं वृषपत्राक्षाद् बिभेति स्त्रीमुखेक्षकात् ॥
40.m: Andhaka would not fear Indra, nor the gods in any way; / how should he fear the bull-eyed one who gazes at the faces of women?"

40.s:
tacchrutvāsya vaco ghoraṃ prahlādaḥ prāha nārada /
na samyaguktaṃ bhavatā viruddhaṃ dharmator'thataḥ //
40.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वास्य वचो घोरं प्रह्लादः प्राह नारद ।
न सम्यगुक्तं भवता विरुद्धं धर्मतोर्ऽथतः ॥
40.m: Hearing his terrible words, Prahlāda said, O Nārada: / "What you have said is not right; it contradicts both righteousness and welfare.

40.s:
hutāśanapataṅgābhyāṃ siṃhakroṣṭukayoriva /
gajendramaśakābhyāṃ ca rukmapāṣāṇayoriva //
40.d:
हुताशनपतङ्गाभ्यां सिंहक्रोष्टुकयोरिव ।
गजेन्द्रमशकाभ्यां च रुक्मपाषाणयोरिव ॥
40.m: As between fire and a moth, or between a lion and a jackal, / or between a lordly elephant and a gnat, or between gold and a stone,

40.s:
eteṣāmebhiruditaṃ yāvadantaramandhaka /
tāvadevāntaraṃ cāsti bhavato vā harasya ca //
40.d:
एतेषामेभिरुदितं यावदन्तरमन्धक ।
तावदेवान्तरं चास्ति भवतो वा हरस्य च ॥
40.m: as great a distance as has been proclaimed between these, O Andhaka, / just so great is the difference between you and Hara.

40.s:
vārito 'si mayā vīra bhūyo bhūyaśca vāryase /
śṛṇuṣva vākyaṃ devarṣerasitasya mahātmanaḥ //
40.d:
वारितो ऽसि मया वीर भूयो भूयश्च वार्यसे ।
शृणुष्व वाक्यं देवर्षेरसितस्य महात्मनः ॥
40.m: You have been warned by me, O hero, and are warned again and again; / listen to the words of the great-souled divine sage Asita:

40.s:
yo dharmaśīlo jitamānaroṣo vidyāvinīto na paropatāpī /
svadāratuṣṭaḥ paradāravarjo natasya loke bhayamasti kiñcit //
40.d:
यो धर्मशीलो जितमानरोषो विद्याविनीतो न परोपतापी ।
स्वदारतुष्टः परदारवर्जो नतस्य लोके भयमस्ति किञ्चित् ॥
40.m: 'He who is virtuous, has conquered pride and anger, is trained in knowledge, harms not others, / is content with his own wife, and shuns the wives of others, has no fear whatsoever in this world.

40.s:
yo dharmahīnaḥ kalahapriyaḥ sadā paropatāpī śrutiśāstravarjitaḥ /
parārthadāreṣsuravarṇasaṃgamī sukhaṃ na vindeta paratra ceha //
40.d:
यो धर्महीनः कलहप्रियः सदा परोपतापी श्रुतिशास्त्रवर्जितः ।
परार्थदारेष्सुरवर्णसंगमी सुखं न विन्देत परत्र चेह ॥
40.m: He who lacks virtue, is ever fond of quarreling, harms others, is devoid of sacred tradition and scripture, / desires the wealth and wives of others, and unites with outcaste women, will find no happiness here or in the hereafter.

40.s: dharmānvito 'bhūnmanurarkaputraḥ svadārasaṃtuṣṭamanāstvagastyaḥ //
40.d: धर्मान्वितो ऽभून्मनुरर्कपुत्रः स्वदारसंतुष्टमनास्त्वगस्त्यः ॥
40.m: Endowed with righteousness was Manu, the son of the Sun; and Agastya had a mind content with his own wife.

40.s:
etāni puṇyāni kṛtānyamībhirmayā nibaddhāni kulakramoktyā /
tejonvitāḥ śāpavarakṣamāśca jātāśca sarve surasiddhapūjyāḥ //
40.d:
एतानि पुण्यानि कृतान्यमीभिर्मया निबद्धानि कुलक्रमोक्त्या ।
तेजोन्विताः शापवरक्षमाश्च जाताश्च सर्वे सुरसिद्धपूज्याः ॥
40.m: These meritorious deeds done by them have been related by me according to lineage; / they became radiant, capable of curses and boons, and revered by gods and Siddhas.

40.s:
adharma'yukto 'ṅgasuto babhūva vibhuśca nityaṃ kalahapriyo 'bhūt /
paropatāpī namucirdurātmā parābalepsurnahuṣaśca rājā //
40.d:
अधर्मऽयुक्तो ऽङ्गसुतो बभूव विभुश्च नित्यं कलहप्रियो ऽभूत् ।
परोपतापी नमुचिर्दुरात्मा पराबलेप्सुर्नहुषश्च राजा ॥
40.m: Joined with unrighteousness was the son of Aṅga, and a ruler who was ever fond of strife; / the wicked Namuci was an afflicter of others, and King Nahuṣa desired the wives of others.

40.s:
parārthalipsurdijito hiraṇyadṛk mūrkhastu tasyāpyanujaḥ sudurmatiḥ /
avarṇasaṃgī yadusttamaujā ete vinaṣṭāstvanayāt purā hi //
40.d:
परार्थलिप्सुर्दिजितो हिरण्यदृक् मूर्खस्तु तस्याप्यनुजः सुदुर्मतिः ।
अवर्णसंगी यदुस्त्तमौजा एते विनष्टास्त्वनयात् पुरा हि ॥
40.m: Hiraṇyadṛk desired the wealth of others, and his younger brother was foolish and evil-minded; / Yadu of mighty valor united with outcaste women; indeed, all these perished through misconduct in former times.

40.s:
tasmād dharmo na saṃtyājyo dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ /
dharmahīnā narā yānti rauravaṃ narakaṃ mahat //
40.d:
तस्माद् धर्मो न संत्याज्यो धर्मो हि परमा गतिः ।
धर्महीना नरा यान्ति रौरवं नरकं महत् ॥
40.m: Therefore righteousness must not be abandoned, for righteousness is the supreme goal; / men devoid of righteousness go to the terrible Raurava hell.

40.s:
dharmastu gaditaḥ puṃbhistāraṇe divi ceha ca /
patanāya tathādharma iha loke paratra ca //
40.d:
धर्मस्तु गदितः पुंभिस्तारणे दिवि चेह च ।
पतनाय तथाधर्म इह लोके परत्र च ॥
40.m: Righteousness has been declared by men for deliverance both in heaven and here, / and likewise unrighteousness for falling, in this world and the hereafter.

40.s:
tyājyaṃ dharmānvitairnnityaṃ paradāropasevanam /
nayanti paradārā hi narakānekaviṃśatim /
sarveṣāmapi varṇānāmeṣa dharmo dhruvo 'ndhaka //
40.d:
त्याज्यं धर्मान्वितैर्न्नित्यं परदारोपसेवनम् ।
नयन्ति परदारा हि नरकानेकविंशतिम् ।
सर्वेषामपि वर्णानामेष धर्मो ध्रुवो ऽन्धक ॥
40.m: Those who possess righteousness must ever abandon dalliance with another's wife; / for the wives of others lead one to twenty-one hells; / this is the eternal duty for all social classes, O Andhaka.

40.s:
parārthaparadāreṣu yadā vāñchāṃ kariṣyati /
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ rauravaṃ bahulāḥ samāḥ //
40.d:
परार्थपरदारेषु यदा वाञ्छां करिष्यति ।
स याति नरकं घोरं रौरवं बहुलाः समाः ॥
40.m: Whenever one directs longing towards another's wealth and another's wife, / he goes to the terrible Raurava hell for many years.'

40.s:
evaṃ purāsurapate devarṣirasito 'vyāyaḥ /
prāha dharmavyavasthānaṃ khagendrāyāruṇāya hi //
40.d:
एवं पुरासुरपते देवर्षिरसितो ऽव्यायः ।
प्राह धर्मव्यवस्थानं खगेन्द्रायारुणाय हि ॥
40.m: Thus in ancient times, O lord of the asuras, the imperishable divine sage Asita / proclaimed the establishment of righteousness to Aruṇa, king of birds.

40.s:
tasmāt sudūrato varjet paradārān vicakṣaṇāḥ /
nayanti nikṛtiprajñaṃ paradārāḥ parābhavam //
40.d:
तस्मात् सुदूरतो वर्जेत् परदारान् विचक्षणाः ।
नयन्ति निकृतिप्रज्ञं परदाराः पराभवम् ॥
40.m: Therefore the wise should avoid the wives of others from afar; / the wives of others bring a deceitful-minded man to destruction."

40.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamukte vacane prahlādaṃ prāha cāndhakaḥ /
bhavān dharmaparastveko nāhaṃ dharma samācare //
40.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने प्रह्लादं प्राह चान्धकः ।
भवान् धर्मपरस्त्वेको नाहं धर्म समाचरे ॥
40.m: Pulastya said: / When these words were spoken, Andhaka said to Prahlāda: / "You alone are devoted to righteousness; I do not practice righteousness!"

40.s:
ityevamuktvā prahlādamandhakaḥ prāha śambaram /
gaccha śambara śailendraṃ mandaraṃ vada śaṅkaram //
40.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा प्रह्लादमन्धकः प्राह शम्बरम् ।
गच्छ शम्बर शैलेन्द्रं मन्दरं वद शङ्करम् ॥
40.m: Having spoken thus to Prahlāda, Andhaka said to Śambara: / "Go, Śambara, to Mandara, the lord of mountains, and say to Śaṅkara:

40.s:
bhikṣo kimarthaṃ śaulendraṃ svargopamyaṃ sakandaram /
paribhuñjasi kenādya tava datto vadasva māma //
40.d:
भिक्षो किमर्थं शौलेन्द्रं स्वर्गोपम्यं सकन्दरम् ।
परिभुञ्जसि केनाद्य तव दत्तो वदस्व माम ॥
40.m: 'O beggar, why do you enjoy the lord of mountains, which resembles heaven with its caves? / Tell me, by whom has it been given to you today?

40.s:
tiṣṭhanti śāsane mahyaṃ devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ /
tat kimarthaṃ nivasase māmanādṛtya mandare //
40.d:
तिष्ठन्ति शासने मह्यं देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः ।
तत् किमर्थं निवससे मामनादृत्य मन्दरे ॥
40.m: The gods, headed by Śakra, abide by my command; / why then do you dwell on Mandara, disregarding me?

40.s:
yadīṣṭastava śailendraḥ kriyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama /
yeyaṃ hi bhavataḥ patnī sā me śīghraṃ pradīyatām //
40.d:
यदीष्टस्तव शैलेन्द्रः क्रियतां वचनं मम ।
येयं हि भवतः पत्नी सा मे शीघ्रं प्रदीयताम् ॥
40.m: If the lord of mountains is dear to you, let my command be done: / that wife of yours—let her be given to me at once!'"

40.s:
ityuktaḥ sa tadā tena śambaro mandaraṃ drutam /
jagāma tatra yatrāste saha devyā pinākadhṛk //
40.d:
इत्युक्तः स तदा तेन शम्बरो मन्दरं द्रुतम् ।
जगाम तत्र यत्रास्ते सह देव्या पिनाकधृक् ॥
40.m: Thus addressed by him then, Śambara went swiftly to Mandara, / where the wielder of the Pināka dwells together with the goddess.

40.s:
gatvovācāndhakavaco yāthātathyaṃ danoḥ sutaḥ /
tamuttaraṃ haraḥ prāha śṛṇvatyā girikanyayā //
40.d:
गत्वोवाचान्धकवचो याथातथ्यं दनोः सुतः ।
तमुत्तरं हरः प्राह शृण्वत्या गिरिकन्यया ॥
40.m: Having arrived, that son of Danu related Andhaka's words accurately; / to him Hara gave this reply while the Daughter of the Mountain was listening:

40.s:
mamāyaṃ mandaro dattaḥ sahasrākṣeṇa dhīmatā /
tanna śaknomyahaṃ tyaktuṃ vinājñāṃ vṛkṣavairiṇaḥ //
40.d:
ममायं मन्दरो दत्तः सहस्राक्षेण धीमता ।
तन्न शक्नोम्यहं त्यक्तुं विनाज्ञां वृक्षवैरिणः ॥
40.m: "This Mandara was given to me by the wise thousand-eyed Indra; / so I cannot abandon it without the command of the enemy of the trees."

40.s:
yaccābravīd dīyatāṃ me giriputrīti dānavaḥ /
tadeṣā yātu svaṃ kāmaṃ nāhaṃ vārayituṃ kṣamaḥ //
40.d:
यच्चाब्रवीद् दीयतां मे गिरिपुत्रीति दानवः ।
तदेषा यातु स्वं कामं नाहं वारयितुं क्षमः ॥
40.m: And as to what the Dānava said, that the mountain's daughter should be given to him: / let her act according to her own wish; I am unable to prevent her.'

40.s:
tato 'bravīt girisutā śambaraṃ munisattama /
brūhi gatvāndhakaṃ vīra mama vākyaṃ vipaścitam //
40.d:
ततो ऽब्रवीत् गिरिसुता शम्बरं मुनिसत्तम ।
ब्रूहि गत्वान्धकं वीर मम वाक्यं विपश्चितम् ॥
40.m: Then the daughter of the mountain said to Śambara, O best of sages: / 'Go, hero, and speak my wise message to Andhaka:

40.s:
ahaṃ patākā saṃgrāme bhavānīśaśca devinau /
prāmadyūtaṃ paristīrya yo jeṣyati sa lapsyate //
40.d:
अहं पताका संग्रामे भवानीशश्च देविनौ ।
प्रामद्यूतं परिस्तीर्य यो जेष्यति स लप्स्यते ॥
40.m: "I am the prize in the battle, and Bhavānī and Īśa are the players. / Setting out the dice-game of combat, whoever wins shall obtain me."'

40.s:
ityevamukto matimān śambaro 'ndakamāgamat /
samāgamyābravīd vākyaṃ śarvagauryośca bhāṣitam //
40.d:
इत्येवमुक्तो मतिमान् शम्बरो ऽन्दकमागमत् ।
समागम्याब्रवीद् वाक्यं शर्वगौर्योश्च भाषितम् ॥
40.m: Being addressed thus, the wise Śambara went to Andhaka; / having approached, he related the words spoken by Śarva and Gaurī.

40.s:
tacchratvā dānavapatiḥ krodhadīptekṣaṇaḥ śvasan /
samāhūyābravīd vākyaṃ duryodhanamidaṃ vacaḥ //
40.d:
तच्छ्रत्वा दानवपतिः क्रोधदीप्तेक्षणः श्वसन् ।
समाहूयाब्रवीद् वाक्यं दुर्योधनमिदं वचः ॥
40.m: Hearing that, the lord of the Dānavas, his eyes blazing with fury, panting, / summoned Duryodhana and spoke these words:

40.s:
gaccha śīghraṃ mahābāho bherīṃ sānnāhikīṃ dṛḍhām /
tāḍayasva suviśrabdhaṃ duḥśīlāmiva yoṣitam //
40.d:
गच्छ शीघ्रं महाबाहो भेरीं सान्नाहिकीं दृढाम् ।
ताडयस्व सुविश्रब्धं दुःशीलामिव योषितम् ॥
40.m: 'Go quickly, O mighty-armed one, and strike firmly the war-drum summoning the army, / beating it without hesitation just like an unchaste woman!'

40.s:
samādiṣṭo 'ndhakenātha bherīṃ duryodhano balāt /
tāḍayāmāsa vegena yathāprāṇena bhūyasā //
40.d:
समादिष्टो ऽन्धकेनाथ भेरीं दुर्योधनो बलात् ।
ताडयामास वेगेन यथाप्राणेन भूयसा ॥
40.m: Thus commanded by Andhaka, Duryodhana / beat the drum violently, forcefully, with all his mighty strength.

40.s:
sā tāḍitā balavatā bherī duryodhanena hi /
satvaraṃ bhairavaṃ rāvaṃ rurāva surabhī yathā //
40.d:
सा ताडिता बलवता भेरी दुर्योधनेन हि ।
सत्वरं भैरवं रावं रुराव सुरभी यथा ॥
40.m: Beaten by the powerful Duryodhana, / the drum quickly sounded forth a terrible roar, like a roaring cow.

40.s:
tasyāstaṃ svaramākarṇya sarva eva mahāsurāḥ /
samāyātāḥ sabhāṃ tūrṇaṃ kimetaditi vādinaḥ //
40.d:
तस्यास्तं स्वरमाकर्ण्य सर्व एव महासुराः ।
समायाताः सभां तूर्णं किमेतदिति वादिनः ॥
40.m: Hearing that sound, all the great asuras / came at once to the assembly, crying out, 'What is this?'

40.s:
yāthātathyaṃ ca tān sarvānāha senāpatirbalī /
te cāpi balināṃ śreṣṭhāḥ sannaddhā yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
40.d:
याथातथ्यं च तान् सर्वानाह सेनापतिर्बली ।
ते चापि बलिनां श्रेष्ठाः सन्नद्धा युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
40.m: The mighty commander-in-chief told them all the facts as they were; / and they, the foremost among the strong, armed themselves, eager for battle.

40.s:
sahāndhakā niryayuste gajairuṣṭrairhayai rathaiḥ /
andhako rathamāsthāya pañcanalvapraṇamāṇataḥ //
40.d:
सहान्धका निर्ययुस्ते गजैरुष्ट्रैर्हयै रथैः ।
अन्धको रथमास्थाय पञ्चनल्वप्रणमाणतः ॥
40.m: Together with Andhaka they marched out with elephants, camels, horses, and chariots. / Andhaka, mounting his chariot measuring five nalvas in size,

40.s:
tryambakaṃ sa parājetuṃ kṛtabuddhirviniryayau /
jambhaḥ kujambho huṇḍaśca tuhuṇḍaḥ śambaro baliḥ //
40.d:
त्र्यम्बकं स पराजेतुं कृतबुद्धिर्विनिर्ययौ ।
जम्भः कुजम्भो हुण्डश्च तुहुण्डः शम्बरो बलिः ॥
40.m: set out, having resolved to conquer Tryambaka: / Jambha, Kujambha, Huṇḍa, Tuhuṇḍa, Śambara, Bali,

40.s:
bāṇāḥ kārtasvaro hastī sūryaśatrurmahodaraḥ /
ayaḥśuṅkuḥ śibiḥ śālvo vṛṣaparvā virocanaḥ //
40.d:
बाणाः कार्तस्वरो हस्ती सूर्यशत्रुर्महोदरः ।
अयःशुङ्कुः शिबिः शाल्वो वृषपर्वा विरोचनः ॥
40.m: Bāṇa, Kārtasvara, Hastin, Sūryaśatru, Mahodara, / Ayaḥśaṅku, Śibi, Śālva, Vṛṣaparvan, Virocana,

40.s:
hayagrīvaḥ kālanemiḥ saṃhlādaḥ kālanāśanaḥ /
śarabhaḥ śalabhaścaiva vipracittiśca vīryavān //
40.d:
हयग्रीवः कालनेमिः संह्लादः कालनाशनः ।
शरभः शलभश्चैव विप्रचित्तिश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
40.m: Hayagrīva, Kālanemi, Saṃhlāda, Kālanāśana, / Śarabha, Śalabha, and the valorous Vipracitti,

40.s:
duryodhanaśca pākaśca vipākaḥ kālaśambarau /
ete cānye ca bahavo mahāvīryā mahābalāḥ /
prajagamurutsukā yoddhuṃ nānāyudhadharā raṇe //
40.d:
दुर्योधनश्च पाकश्च विपाकः कालशम्बरौ ।
एते चान्ये च बहवो महावीर्या महाबलाः ।
प्रजगमुरुत्सुका योद्धुं नानायुधधरा रणे ॥
40.m: Duryodhana, Pāka, Vipāka, and Kālaśambara; / these and many others of great prowess and mighty power, / bearing various weapons, marched forth eager to fight in the battle.

40.s:
itthaṃ durātmā danusainyapālastadāndhako yoddhumanā hareṇa /
mahācalaṃ mandaramabhyupeyivān sa kālapāśāvasito hi mandadhīḥ //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe catvāriśo 'dhyāyaḥ
40.d:
इत्थं दुरात्मा दनुसैन्यपालस्तदान्धको योद्धुमना हरेण ।
महाचलं मन्दरमभ्युपेयिवान् स कालपाशावसितो हि मन्दधीः ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे चत्वारिशो ऽध्यायः
40.m:
Thus that wicked commander of the Danu army, Andhaka, intending to fight Hara, / advanced toward the great mountain Mandara, dull-witted and caught in the noose of Time.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter in the holy Vāmana Purāṇa.

41.s:
pulāstya uvāca /
haro 'pi śambare yāte samāhūyātha nandinam /
prāhāmantraya śailāde ye sthitāstava śāsane //
41.d:
पुलास्त्य उवाच ।
हरो ऽपि शम्बरे याते समाहूयाथ नन्दिनम् ।
प्राहामन्त्रय शैलादे ये स्थितास्तव शासने ॥
41.m: Pulastya said: / 'When Śambara had gone, Hara summoned Nandin / and said: "O son of Śilāda, summon those who abide under your command."

41.s:
tato maheśavacanānnandī tūrṇataraṃ gataḥ /
upaspṛśya jalaṃ śrīmān sasmāra gaṇanāyakān //
41.d:
ततो महेशवचनान्नन्दी तूर्णतरं गतः ।
उपस्पृश्य जलं श्रीमान् सस्मार गणनायकान् ॥
41.m: Then, at the word of Maheśvara, Nandin went with great speed; / sipping water, the glorious one remembered the leaders of the hosts.

41.s:
nandinā saṃsmṛtāḥ sarve gaṇanāthāḥ sahasraśaḥ /
samutpatya tvarāyuktāḥ praṇatāstridaseśvaram //
41.d:
नन्दिना संस्मृताः सर्वे गणनाथाः सहस्रशः ।
समुत्पत्य त्वरायुक्ताः प्रणतास्त्रिदसेश्वरम् ॥
41.m: Remembered by Nandin, all the leaders of the hosts in their thousands / rose up in haste and bowed down to the lord of the gods.

41.s:
āgatāṃśca gaṇānnandī kṛtāñjalipuṭo 'vyayaḥ /
sarvān nivedayāmāsa śaṅkarāya mahātmane //
41.d:
आगतांश्च गणान्नन्दी कृताञ्जलिपुटो ऽव्ययः ।
सर्वान् निवेदयामास शङ्कराय महात्मने ॥
41.m: And the imperishable Nandin, with folded palms, / presented all the arrived hosts to the great-souled Śaṅkara.

41.s:
nandyuvāca /
yānetān paśyase śaṃbho trinetrāñjaṭilāñśucīn /
ete rudrā iti khyātāḥ koṭya ekādaśaiva tu //
41.d:
नन्द्युवाच ।
यानेतान् पश्यसे शंभो त्रिनेत्राञ्जटिलाञ्शुचीन् ।
एते रुद्रा इति ख्याताः कोट्य एकादशैव तु ॥
41.m: Nandin said: / "These whom you see, O Śambhu, three-eyed, matted-haired, and pure, / are known as the Rudras, eleven crores in number.

41.s:
vānarāsyān paśyase yān śārdūlasamavikramān /
eteṣāṃ dvārapālāste mannamāno yaśodhanāḥ //
41.d:
वानरास्यान् पश्यसे यान् शार्दूलसमविक्रमान् ।
एतेषां द्वारपालास्ते मन्नमानो यशोधनाः ॥
41.m: Those whom you see with monkey faces, having prowess like tigers, / rich in renown and bearing my name, are their gatekeepers.

41.s:
ṣaṇmukhān paśyase yāṃśca śaktipāṇīñśikhidhvajān /
ṣaṭ ca ṣaṣṭistathā koṭyaḥ skandanāmnaḥ kumārakān //
41.d:
षण्मुखान् पश्यसे यांश्च शक्तिपाणीञ्शिखिध्वजान् ।
षट् च षष्टिस्तथा कोट्यः स्कन्दनाम्नः कुमारकान् ॥
41.m: And those whom you see six-faced, holding lances, with peacock banners, / sixty-six crores in number, are the youths bearing the name of Skanda.

41.s:
etāvatyastathā koṭya śākhā nāma ṣaḍānanāḥ /
viśākhāstāvadevoktā naigameyāśca śaṅkara //
41.d:
एतावत्यस्तथा कोट्य शाखा नाम षडाननाः ।
विशाखास्तावदेवोक्ता नैगमेयाश्च शङ्कर ॥
41.m: As many crores are the six-faced ones named Śākhas; / just as many are declared to be the Viśākhas and the Naigameyas, O Śaṅkara.

41.s:
saptakoṭiśataṃ śaṃbho amī vai pramathottamāḥ /
ekaikaṃ prati deveśa tāvatyo hyapi mātaraḥ //
41.d:
सप्तकोटिशतं शंभो अमी वै प्रमथोत्तमाः ।
एकैकं प्रति देवेश तावत्यो ह्यपि मातरः ॥
41.m: O Śambhu, these seven hundred crores are the foremost Pramathas; / and for every single one of them, O lord of gods, there are just as many Mothers.

41.s:
bhasmāruṇitadehāśca trinetrāḥ śūlapāṇayaḥ /
ete śaivā iti proktāstava bhaktā gaṇeśvarāḥ //
41.d:
भस्मारुणितदेहाश्च त्रिनेत्राः शूलपाणयः ।
एते शैवा इति प्रोक्तास्तव भक्ता गणेश्वराः ॥
41.m: Their bodies reddened with ash, three-eyed and holding tridents in hand, / these are called Śaivas, lords of the hosts devoted to you.

41.s:
tathā pāśupatāścānye bhasmaprahāraṇā vibho /
ete gaṇāstvasaṃkhyātāḥ sahāyārthaṃ samāgatāḥ //
41.d:
तथा पाशुपताश्चान्ये भस्मप्रहारणा विभो ।
एते गणास्त्वसंख्याताः सहायार्थं समागताः ॥
41.m: Likewise, others are the Pāśupatas, O all-pervading lord, wielding ash as their weapon; / these innumerable hosts have arrived to assist you.

41.s:
pinākadhāriṇo raudrā gaṇāḥ kālamukhāpare /
tava bhaktāḥ samāyātā jaṭāmaṇḍalinodbhutāḥ //
41.d:
पिनाकधारिणो रौद्रा गणाः कालमुखापरे ।
तव भक्ताः समायाता जटामण्डलिनोद्भुताः ॥
41.m: Terrible, wielding the Pināka, other hosts are the Kālamukhas; / devoted to you, having masses of matted hair, they have arrived.

41.s:
khaṭvāṅgayodhino vīrā raktacarmasamāvṛtāḥ /
ime prāptā gaṇā yoddhuṃ mahāvratina uttamāḥ //
41.d:
खट्वाङ्गयोधिनो वीरा रक्तचर्मसमावृताः ।
इमे प्राप्ता गणा योद्धुं महाव्रतिन उत्तमाः ॥
41.m: Warriors fighting with skull-staffs, covered with red hides, / these foremost observers of the great vow have arrived to fight.

41.s:
digvāsaso mauninaśca ghaṇṭāpraharaṇāstathā /
nirāśrayā nāma gaṇāḥ samāyātā jagadguro //
41.d:
दिग्वाससो मौनिनश्च घण्टाप्रहरणास्तथा ।
निराश्रया नाम गणाः समायाता जगद्गुरो ॥
41.m: Clothed in the quarters, keeping silence, and bearing bells as weapons, / the hosts called Nirāśrayas have arrived, O teacher of the universe.

41.s:
sārdhadvinetrāḥ padmākṣāḥ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasaḥ /
samāyātāḥ khagārūḍhā vṛṣabhadhvajino 'vyayāḥ //
41.d:
सार्धद्विनेत्राः पद्माक्षाः श्रीवत्साङ्कितवक्षसः ।
समायाताः खगारूढा वृषभध्वजिनो ऽव्ययाः ॥
41.m: Having two and a half eyes, lotus-eyed, their chests marked with the Śrīvatsa, / mounted on birds, carrying bull-banners, imperishable,

41.s:
mahāpāśupatā nāma cakraśūladharāstathā /
bhairavo viṣṇunā sārddhamabhedenārcito hi yai //
41.d:
महापाशुपता नाम चक्रशूलधरास्तथा ।
भैरवो विष्णुना सार्द्धमभेदेनार्चितो हि यै ॥
41.m: called the Mahāpāśupatas, wielding the discus and the trident, / by whom Bhairava is worshipped without distinction along with Viṣṇu.

41.s:
ime mṛgondravadanāḥ śūlabāṇadhanurdharāḥ /
gaṇāstvadromasaṃbhūtā vīrabhadrapurogamāḥ //
41.d:
इमे मृगोन्द्रवदनाः शूलबाणधनुर्धराः ।
गणास्त्वद्रोमसंभूता वीरभद्रपुरोगमाः ॥
41.m: These have lion faces, holding tridents, arrows, and bows; / they are the hosts born from your body hair, led by Vīrabhadra.

41.s:
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ /
sahāyārthaṃ tavāyātā yathāprītyādiśasva tān //
41.d:
एते चान्ये च बहवः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।
सहायार्थं तवायाता यथाप्रीत्यादिशस्व तान् ॥
41.m: These and many others, in hundreds and in thousands, / have arrived to assist you; command them as it pleases you."

41.s:
tato 'bhyetya gaṇāḥ sarve praṇemurvṛṣabhadhvajam /
tān kareṇaiva bhagavān samāśvāsyopaveśayat //
41.d:
ततो ऽभ्येत्य गणाः सर्वे प्रणेमुर्वृषभध्वजम् ।
तान् करेणैव भगवान् समाश्वास्योपवेशयत् ॥
41.m: Then, drawing near, all the hosts bowed to the one whose banner is a bull; / the Lord consoled them with his hand and made them sit down.

41.s:
mahāpāśupatān dṛṣṭvā samutthāya maheśvaraḥ /
saṃpariṣvajatādhyakṣāṃste praṇemurmaheśvaram //
41.d:
महापाशुपतान् दृष्ट्वा समुत्थाय महेश्वरः ।
संपरिष्वजताध्यक्षांस्ते प्रणेमुर्महेश्वरम् ॥
41.m: Seeing the Mahāpāśupatas, Maheśvara arose / and embraced their chiefs; and they bowed down to Maheśvara.

41.s: tatastadadbhutatamaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve gaṇeśvarāḥ suciraṃ vismitākṣāśca vailakṣyamagamat param //
41.d: ततस्तदद्भुततमं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे गणेश्वराः सुचिरं विस्मिताक्षाश्च वैलक्ष्यमगमत् परम् ॥
41.m: Then, seeing that most wonderful deed, all the lords of the hosts, their eyes wide with amazement for a long time, fell into utter bewilderment.

41.s:
vismitākṣān gaṇān dṛṣṭvā sailadiryogināṃ varaḥ /
prāha prahasya deveśaṃ śūlapāṇiṃ gaṇādhipam //
41.d:
विस्मिताक्षान् गणान् दृष्ट्वा सैलदिर्योगिनां वरः ।
प्राह प्रहस्य देवेशं शूलपाणिं गणाधिपम् ॥
41.m: Seeing the hosts with wondering eyes, the son of Śilāda, foremost among yogins, / smiled and said to the lord of gods, the trident-handed master of the hosts:

41.s:
vismitāmī gaṇā deva sarva eva maheśvara /
mahāpāśupatānāṃ hi yat tvayāliṅganaṃ kṛtam //
41.d:
विस्मितामी गणा देव सर्व एव महेश्वर ।
महापाशुपतानां हि यत् त्वयालिङ्गनं कृतम् ॥
41.m: 'All these hosts, O god, O Maheśvara, are astonished / at the embrace that was given by you to the Mahāpāśupatas.

41.s:
tadeteṣāṃ mahādeva sphuṭaṃ trailokyavindakam /
rūpaṃ jñānaṃ vivekaṃ ca vadasva svecchayā vibho //
41.d:
तदेतेषां महादेव स्फुटं त्रैलोक्यविन्दकम् ।
रूपं ज्ञानं विवेकं च वदस्व स्वेच्छया विभो ॥
41.m: Therefore, O Mahādeva, clearly declare, according to your will, O lord, / their form, wisdom, and discernment which enlighten the three worlds.'

41.s:
pramathādhipatervākyaṃ viditvā bhūtabhāvanaḥ /
babhāṣe tān gaṇān sarvān bhāvābhāvavicāriṇaḥ //
41.d:
प्रमथाधिपतेर्वाक्यं विदित्वा भूतभावनः ।
बभाषे तान् गणान् सर्वान् भावाभावविचारिणः ॥
41.m: Understanding the words of the lord of the Pramathas, the creator of all beings / addressed all those hosts who contemplate existence and non-existence.

41.s:
rudra uvāca/ /
bhavdbhirbhaktisaṃyuktairharo bhāvena pūjitaḥ /
ahaṅkāravimūḍhaiśca nindadbhirvaiṣṇavaṃ padam //
41.d:
रुद्र उवाच। ।
भव्द्भिर्भक्तिसंयुक्तैर्हरो भावेन पूजितः ।
अहङ्कारविमूढैश्च निन्दद्भिर्वैष्णवं पदम् ॥
41.m:
Rudra said:
“Hara has been worshipped with devotion and affection by you,
who are also deluded by egoism and revile the status of Viṣṇu.

41.s:
tenājñānena bhavatonādṛtyānuvirodhitāḥ /
yo 'haṃ sa bhagavān viṣṇurviṣṇuryaḥ so 'hamavyayaḥ //
41.d:
तेनाज्ञानेन भवतोनादृत्यानुविरोधिताः ।
यो ऽहं स भगवान् विष्णुर्विष्णुर्यः सो ऽहमव्ययः ॥
41.m:
Because of that ignorance, those who are disregarded by you are opposed.
Whoever I am, that is the Lord Viṣṇu; and whoever is Viṣṇu, that imperishable one am I.

41.s:
nāvayorvai viśeṣo 'sti ekā mūrtirdvidhā sthitā /
tadamībhirnaravyāghrairbhaktibhāvayutairgaṇaiḥ //
41.d:
नावयोर्वै विशेषो ऽस्ति एका मूर्तिर्द्विधा स्थिता ।
तदमीभिर्नरव्याघ्रैर्भक्तिभावयुतैर्गणैः ॥
41.m:
There is indeed no difference between us two; one form stands divided in two.
Therefore, by these attendants, tigers among men, endowed with devotion,

41.s:
yathāhaṃ vai parijñāto na bhavadbhistathā dhruvam /
yenāhaṃ nindito nityaṃ bhavadbhirmūḍhabuddhibhiḥ //
41.d:
यथाहं वै परिज्ञातो न भवद्भिस्तथा ध्रुवम् ।
येनाहं निन्दितो नित्यं भवद्भिर्मूढबुद्धिभिः ॥
41.m:
just as I am truly known, surely you have not known Me in that manner;
for I have been continually reviled by you of foolish minds.

41.s:
tena jñānaṃ hi vai naṣṭaṃ nātastvāliṅgitā mayā /
ityevamukte vacane gaṇāḥ procurmaheśvaram //
41.d:
तेन ज्ञानं हि वै नष्टं नातस्त्वालिङ्गिता मया ।
इत्येवमुक्ते वचने गणाः प्रोचुर्महेश्वरम् ॥
41.m:
Therefore, your knowledge is indeed lost; hence you have not been embraced by Me.”
When this statement was made, the attendants spoke to Maheśvara.

41.s:
kathaṃ bhavān yathaikyena saṃsthito 'sti janārdanaḥ /
bhavān hi nirmalaḥ suddhaḥ śāntaḥ suklo nirañjanaḥ //
41.d:
कथं भवान् यथैक्येन संस्थितो ऽस्ति जनार्दनः ।
भवान् हि निर्मलः सुद्धः शान्तः सुक्लो निरञ्जनः ॥
41.m:
kathaṃ bhavān yathaikyena saṃsthito 'sti janārdanaḥ
bhavān hi nirmalaḥ suddhaḥ śāntaḥ suklo nirañjanaḥ

41.s:
sa cāpyañjanasaṃkāśaḥ kathaṃ teneha yujyate /
teṣāṃ vacanamarthāḍhyaṃ śrutvā jīmūtavāhanaḥ //
41.d:
स चाप्यञ्जनसंकाशः कथं तेनेह युज्यते ।
तेषां वचनमर्थाढ्यं श्रुत्वा जीमूतवाहनः ॥
41.m:
sa cāpyañjanasaṃkāśaḥ kathaṃ teneha yujyate
teṣāṃ vacanamarthāḍhyaṃ śrutvā jīmūtavāhanaḥ

41.s:
vihasya meghagambhīraṃ gaṇānidamuvāca ha /
śrūyatāṃ sarvamākhyāsye svayaśovarddhanaṃ vacaḥ //
41.d:
विहस्य मेघगम्भीरं गणानिदमुवाच ह ।
श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये स्वयशोवर्द्धनं वचः ॥
41.m:
vihasya meghagambhīraṃ gaṇānidamuvāca ha
śrūyatāṃ sarvamākhyāsye svayaśovarddhanaṃ vacaḥ

41.s:
na tveva yogyā yūyaṃ hi mahājñānasya karhicit /
apavādabhayād guhyaṃ bhavatāṃ hi prakāśaye //
41.d:
न त्वेव योग्या यूयं हि महाज्ञानस्य कर्हिचित् ।
अपवादभयाद् गुह्यं भवतां हि प्रकाशये ॥
41.m:
na tveva yogyā yūyaṃ hi mahājñānasya karhicit
apavādabhayād guhyaṃ bhavatāṃ hi prakāśaye

41.s:
priyadhvamapi caitena yanmaccittāstu nityaśaḥ /
ekarūpātmakaṃ dehaṃ kurudhyaṃ yatnamāsthitāḥ //
41.d:
प्रियध्वमपि चैतेन यन्मच्चित्तास्तु नित्यशः ।
एकरूपात्मकं देहं कुरुध्यं यत्नमास्थिताः ॥
41.m:
priyadhvamapi caitena yanmaccittāstu nityaśaḥ
ekarūpātmakaṃ dehaṃ kurudhyaṃ yatnamāsthitāḥ

41.s:
payasā haviṣādyaiśca snāpanena prayatnataḥ /
candanādibhirekāgrairna me prītiḥ prajāyate //
41.d:
पयसा हविषाद्यैश्च स्नापनेन प्रयत्नतः ।
चन्दनादिभिरेकाग्रैर्न मे प्रीतिः प्रजायते ॥
41.m:
payasā haviṣādyaiśca snāpanena prayatnataḥ
candanādibhirekāgrairna me prītiḥ prajāyate

41.s:
yatnāt krakacamādāya chindadhvaṃ mama vigraham /
narakārhā bhavadbhaktā rakṣāmi svayaśor'thataḥ //
41.d:
यत्नात् क्रकचमादाय छिन्दध्वं मम विग्रहम् ।
नरकार्हा भवद्भक्ता रक्षामि स्वयशोर्ऽथतः ॥
41.m:
yatnāt krakacamādāya chindadhvaṃ mama vigraham
narakārhā bhavadbhaktā rakṣāmi svayaśor'thataḥ

41.s:
māyaṃ vadiṣyate loko mahāntamapavādinam /
yathā patanti narake harabhaktāstapasvinaḥ //
41.d:
मायं वदिष्यते लोको महान्तमपवादिनम् ।
यथा पतन्ति नरके हरभक्तास्तपस्विनः ॥
41.m:
māyaṃ vadiṣyate loko mahāntamapavādinam
yathā patanti narake harabhaktāstapasvinaḥ

41.s:
vrajanti narakaṃ ghoraṃ ityevaṃ parivādinaḥ /
ator'thaṃ na kṣipāmyadya bhavato narake 'dbhute //
41.d:
व्रजन्ति नरकं घोरं इत्येवं परिवादिनः ।
अतोर्ऽथं न क्षिपाम्यद्य भवतो नरके ऽद्भुते ॥
41.m:
vrajanti narakaṃ ghoraṃ ityevaṃ parivādinaḥ
ator'thaṃ na kṣipāmyadya bhavato narake 'dbhute

41.s:
yannindadhvaṃ jagannāthaṃ puṣkarākṣaṃ ca manmayam /
sa caiva sadṛśo loke vidyate sacarācare /
śvetamūrtiḥ sa gavān pīto rakto 'ñjanaprabhaḥ //
41.d:
यन्निन्दध्वं जगन्नाथं पुष्कराक्षं च मन्मयम् ।
स चैव सदृशो लोके विद्यते सचराचरे ।
श्वेतमूर्तिः स गवान् पीतो रक्तो ऽञ्जनप्रभः ॥
41.m:
